chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts and asks everyone to silence electronic devices. Staff directs anyone who has not signed up for testimony to see the sergeant at arms at the back.
chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing and gives testimony sign-up instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.speaker: Council Staff

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Chair Gennaro convenes the oversight hearing on DEP's citizen enforcement programs and the accompanying legislation. He lists Intros 11-A, 48, 561-A, 562, 869-A, and the preconsidered Department of Finance fleet bill.
chapters.title: Gennaro opens hearing and lists six idling and noise bills

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Good afternoon, I'm Councilmember Jim Gennaro, Chair of the Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Today we'll be holding an oversight hearing on DEP's citizen enforcement programs, as well as the following legislation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 11A, sponsored by Speaker Julie Menon, in relation to increasing civil penalties for idling infractions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 48, sponsored by Councilmember Aviles, we'll be hearing from her, in relation to translating the Citizen Air Complaint Program portal into designated citywide languages.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: A pre-considered bill sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson in relation to idling violations in...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: DOF's, DOF?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Is that finance?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: In relation to the Department of Finance's fleet program and three bills that I have sponsored.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Proposed Intro 561A in relation to regulating the idling of engines and the use of citizens'complaints to enforce...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Idling laws propose Intro 869A in relation to establishing a code of conduct

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: applicable to citizen noise complaints and Intro 562 in relation to establishing a program that transfers liability for certain engine idling violations to lessees of vehicles.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says city air quality has improved through Council action on heating oil, commercial cooking emissions, and the city fleet. He describes the phase-out of No. 6 and No. 4 oil and notes idling complaints rose from about 9,000 in 2019 to 163,000 in 2025.
chapters.title: Gennaro recounts clean-air history and idling complaint growth

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the city's air quality has improved over the last 20 years, thanks in no small part to the council.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Over that time, the council has passed legislation to phase out dirty heating oil, regulating emissions from certain commercial cooking equipment.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Making the city fleet electric and reducing emissions from certain types of buildings.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Each of these laws has demonstrated the council's commitment to making the air cleaner and safer for New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: While the air quality has improved, there is still work to be done, work that this committee takes very seriously.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Let me just go off script for a second and talk about some of the things that have happened.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I remember in one fell swoop, the council working with the state eliminated

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: the dirtiest fuel oil, number six oil.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So six oil went out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Number four oil, many of you people know what that is.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's a blend of number two and number six.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That was reduced from a sulfur content.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: between like 3,000 and 4,000 down to 1,000 or 1,500 or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So it made four cleaner.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And in conjunction with the state, we made number two ultra-low...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, we met at ultra-low sulfur, ULSD, and we did something.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, and then we, there was some other component to that, but those measures taken together,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: clean the city's air quality to the equivalent of taking every car, truck, and bus off the road forever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, that was a good thing, but we have to keep going, and idling is a very big deal.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just thought I'd give you that little piece of history.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, back to script.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says motor vehicles contribute about 11% of local fine particulate matter and 28% of nitrogen oxide emissions. He links those emissions to premature deaths and emergency visits and says communities of color face disproportionately high diesel pollution.
chapters.title: Gennaro details PM2.5 and NOx health burdens in EJ communities

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Every year, motor vehicles contribute approximately 11% of the local fine particulate matter.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: By that, we mean PM2.5.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: People who know air pollution know it, PM2.5, PM10, all that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Where was I?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And 28% of the local nitrogen oxide emissions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: These emissions are harmful to human health, leading to hundreds of premature deaths and emergency department visits for respiratory and cardiovascular disease every year.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's more...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's more, communities of color are subjected to as much as 15% more fine particulate matter pollution from diesel trucks in a neighborhood with the greatest levels of pollution attributable emergency department visits are all EJ neighborhoods.

chapters.summary: Gennaro explains that idling is limited to one minute near schools or parks and three minutes elsewhere. He says the 2019 Citizen Air Complaint Portal made enforcement easier and that stakeholders have asked for reforms since 2024.
chapters.title: Gennaro explains idling law and Air Complaint Portal expansion

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: To address these air quality concerns, the New York City Air Code prohibits motor vehicles from idling for longer than one minute near a school or a park and for longer than three minutes elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Although a citizen complaint program process for these air code provisions has existed in local law since 1971,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: to better facilitate participation in the citizen complaint program, in 2019, the city established the City Air Complaint Portal, which allowed the public to more easily submit evidence of idling to DEP.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Since then, the number of idling complaints submitted each year has been climbing dramatically, from 9,070

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: complaints submitted in 2019 to 163,090 complaints submitted in 2025.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: In that time, stakeholders, including DEP, have called upon the Council to reform this program to make it more efficient and fairer for all involved.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As evidenced by the committee's hearing on citizen enforcement program and accompanying legislation in 2024, and again today, when did we last hear this bill?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so we last heard this bill in 2024.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And again today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I am committed, as is this committee, to doing our best to make this program easier and fairer for all parties while maintaining the Council's ultimate goal of reducing harmful air pollution.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says DEP, OATH, and the Department of Finance were invited but declined to testify. He criticizes DEP's short written submission and says he will read it into the record, while expressing disappointment at the agencies' absence.
chapters.title: Gennaro criticizes DEP, OATH, and DOF for declining testimony

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That leads us to today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And although we invited DEP, OATH, the Office of Administrative Trials and

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I guess, and the Department of Finance to provide testimony about the Citizen Enforcement Program and the proposed legislation being heard today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And despite DEP's previous insistence that the Council make reforms to this program, as you can see, they have declined the invitation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then DEP has provided a page and a half of testimony without much substance.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I will be reading that into the record.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Feel free to giggle as I read it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And no word from Oath or DOF.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The giggle part I just made up.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's not written down, okay?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I hope that moving forward, the administration can show a bit more respect to this institution and the important role we play in oversight and lawmaking.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: While I'm disappointed by their absence, I look forward from hearing from you all today about your experience.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: With the Citizen Enforcement Program and your suggestions to make it better.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for taking the time out of your day to make this a fruitful hearing with your good and thorough testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hopefully the agencies will be listening in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, we got the person right there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I'm sure they're listening in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm sure they're like, you were giggling when I said giggling.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: They're not giggling.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: They're grimacing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So hopefully the agency will be listening in and taking notes.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We certainly will.

chapters.summary: Council Member Aviles says Intro 48 would translate the Citizen Air Complaint Portal into designated citywide languages. She argues idling pollution disproportionately harms environmental justice communities and that limited English proficiency locks residents out of enforcement.
chapters.title: Aviles presents Intro 48 as language-justice measure

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gennaro, for always being very generous and lovely with your comments.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you to the members of the committee, members of the public who have joined us here today.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Today, the committee will hear one of my bills, Intro 48, which brings language justice to the fight for clean air in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Idling vehicles are a major contributor of air pollution in our city.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Cars and trucks idling on New York City streets produce 130,000 tons of carbon dioxide a year.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: The consequences of this pollution are deadly, resulting in 2,400 deaths each year in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: We see a disproportionate impact in communities like mine, environmental justice communities that bear the brunt.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Of an enormous amount of siting of polluting infrastructures and certainly trucks.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: The Citizen Air Complaint Program has been a critical tool to boost enforcement capacity for the city's idling law.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: This program allows everyday New Yorkers to take on

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: corporate polluters who harm their communities.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Early this year, the city recovered $9 million from Amazon alone for one year, one of the city's most flagrant polluters.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: In a time where the federal government and the state government are rolling back

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: environmental protections, it is a moment for the city to lean forward, 10 toes down, to strengthen and expand our programs that protect our residents.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: The Citizens Complaint Portal is a vital tool for improving our city's air quality,

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: But the fact that complaints must only be submitted in English

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: limits its ability to deliver true environmental justice for our city, where nearly a quarter of the residents have limited English proficiency.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: In fact, in my district, we are a majority foreign-born.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: district.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: 70 plus of my residents speak Spanish or Mandarin or Cantonese.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: They are effectively locked out from caring for their neighbors in this program.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: My bill, Intro 48, would require DP to translate the portal into each of these cities'designated citywide languages.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: This bill is a step forward in addressing the deadly inequities of environmental justice communities that they currently face.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I thank the 38 council members who have signed on to Intro 48 and encourage my colleagues to join in the fight for language justice and co-sponsor this bill and ensure that we have the strongest

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: citizen complaint program and can do everything in our power to hold polluters accountable in our city.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

chapters.summary: Gennaro reads DEP Commissioner Lisa Garcia's written testimony into the record. The statement explains that the civilian complaint program lets the public submit evidence of idling, dust, and noise violations and receive a share of penalties.
chapters.title: Gennaro reads DEP testimony on citizen complaint process

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Because we have two, you know, it's going to be a balance.

utterances.text: All right, well, okay, so from now on, no talking during this hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: There will be no testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: There will be nothing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We will just sit and meditate, you know, and until the baby's, like, safely asleep.

utterances.text: Okay, here we go.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Testimony of Lisa Garcia, Commissioner, DEP for RVA, yeah, yeah, yeah.

utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairman Gennaro, members of the Environmental Protection and Waterfronts Committee.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I am Lisa Garcia, Commissioner of DEP.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm happy to provide some information about the operation of our citizen complaint program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: However, on the advice of counsel and related litigation, I will not be in attendance at the hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And at this time, I'll not provide comments on Intro 11A or Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sip of water, that's what it says in here, so I'll follow it.

chapters.summary: The DEP statement says two staff including a supervisor review each submission and that DEP issued about 102,000 idling summonses in 2025. It says DEP now receives about 700 idling reports daily and has a backlog of roughly 230,000 videos.
chapters.title: DEP testimony describes 2025 complaint volume and 230,000-video backlog

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: New York City's civilian complaint program allows anyone to record and submit evidence of certain idling, dust, and sound reproduction device violations, and then receive a share of the penalties collected if the evidence results in a violation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: These programs have become increasingly popular in recent years, particularly the program for idling enforcement.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I got a little frog in my throat here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Had a sticky bun.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Maybe that's it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And it has a chart here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Talks about complaints submitted, you know, and it's a lot of numbers.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Numbers issued, whatever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm not going to do the charts.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: To participate in the idling program, anyone can log into the air complaint system on the DEP website and submit a video of the idling with a description of the incident.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Two DEP staff, including a supervisor, review each submission to determine whether there is evidence of a violation and issue summonses when sufficient evidence is observed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Either DEP or the citizen can pursue the complaint.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If DEP pursues, we issue summonses after the review when sufficient evidence is observed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If the citizen pursues, they issue the summons themselves.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The summons leads to a hearing before oath.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: person who submitted the complaint is informed of the hearing date and can follow the progress of their submission through the air complaint system.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Anybody got a cough drop?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Anybody?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, Ricola.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Now we're talking.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Where are we?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: In 2025, DEP reviewed more than 163,000 submissions from the public and issued about 102,000 summonses for idling, almost 300 summonses issued per day.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As the council is aware, this has been an exponential increase over just a few years.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then there's a little question mark between the two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I don't know what that means.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Currently, DEP receives about 700 idling reports per day.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Each is reviewed by a DEP inspector and supervisor.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We have a current backlog of about 230,000 videos that DEP must review.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: DP received 21 new lines, you know, personnel lines, approved as part of the FY27 November plan.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: These new positions include air pollution inspectors, clerical associates, principal administrative associates, and one certified IT developer.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Seven inspectors recently started.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We are working with the Department of Citywide Administrative Services and the Office of Management and Budget to bring the rest on as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Citizen complaints are adjudicated at oath, which also support the processing of payments.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The council should consider the operational impacts in adjudicating and processing citizen complaints of these cases when making changes to the law.

chapters.summary: DEP says it is already compliant with Intro 48 because its website has translated instructions. It raises concerns about Intro 562 shifting liability to lessees, supports the intent of Intro 869, and defers to the Department of Finance on the fleet bill.
chapters.title: DEP testimony comments on Intros 48, 562, 869, and fleet bill

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Six pieces of legislation are being heard today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The details of some of these bills relate to current litigation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Therefore, I cannot speak to items in the bills that touch on legal issues being litigated.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But they do have, you know, thoughts on some other bills, and I'm going to read those now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 48 requires that the Citizens Air Complaint website and its components be available in the designated citywide languages.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The DEP is already compliant with the bill.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Because the website currently has instructions and translations in all of the designated citywide languages, we encourage New Yorkers of all backgrounds to participate in the compliant program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just reading what's on the paper.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 562.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: 562 would establish a program that transfers liability for certain engine idling violations to lessees of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: DEP issues summonses to vehicle owners based on the license plate or other identifying information on the vehicle seen idling.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The evidence we received does not indicate who is driving the vehicle at the time of the violation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Often there isn't any driver present.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If the vehicle is leased, that is also not indicated in the evidence collected.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We have concerns.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: concerns about this proposal, such as removing the vehicle owner's incentive to install anti-idling equipment in vehicles.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 869.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Intro 869 would establish a code of conduct applicable to citizen noise compliance.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We appreciate and support the intent of this bill.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Additionally,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oath already has rules of conduct for citizen complainants that are strictly enforced when adjudicating these matters.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Preconsidered Bill T-2026-2662.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The preconsidered bill requires the Department of Finance.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: To provide DEP a list of companies and registration plates enrolled in its fleet program

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: and requires DEP to send DOF a list of all idling notices of violation issued for vehicles enrolled in the fleet program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We are reviewing this legislation with our colleagues at the Department of Finance.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I defer to them for discussion about their concerns.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony today.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says the committee will now hear from public witnesses and reads the formal rules on decorum, witness tables, recording, and written testimony. He says speakers will generally have two minutes and can submit written testimony within 72 hours.
chapters.title: Gennaro opens public comment and reads hearing rules

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, we got that out of the way.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And now we're going to start hearing from real people.

utterances.text: I think it's, what am I doing here?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.text: Thank you, Harvey.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Public comment period.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: At the beginning of the public comment period, oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's just a note saying that I have to read this.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, let me just go with what I have to read.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I remind members of the public that this is a formal government proceeding, sort of, and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As such, members of the public shall remain silent at all times.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, I guess, except when they're testifying.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the Sergeant-at-Arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you wish to speak at today's hearing, please fill out an appearance card with the Sergeant-at-Arms and wait to be recognized.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: When recognized, you will have two minutes to speak on today's hearing topic, DEP citizen enforcement programs and accompanying legislation to be heard today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, because this is also an oversight hearing as well as a legislative hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you have a written statement or additional testimony you wish to submit for the record, please submit a copy of that testimony to the Sergeant at Arms.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You may also email.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: email written testimony to testimony at council, C-O-U-N-C-I-L, .nyc.gov within 72 hours of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Audio and video recordings will not be accepted.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says he instructed staff to arrange panels fairly so both sides are heard and no group waits hours. He says he plays no role in deciding who testifies first and trusts staff to order the panels.
chapters.title: Gennaro explains staff controls panel order

utterances.text: I'm about to call the first panel, and I want to...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I want to note that, you know, when it comes to arranging the panels,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I've instructed, as I always do, the staff to arrange, you know, the panels in such a way

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: that it is fair and we get both sides and one group doesn't have to wait three hours to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I want it known for the record that I play no role whatsoever in figuring out who's testifying when, what panels are first or last or whatever that is left to staff.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Aviles says DEP has translated a form or guidance but not integrated translation into the portal. She says users must print a form, return to the website, and manually translate each part, which she calls unworkable and not full language access.
chapters.title: Aviles rebuts DEP claim that portal is already translated

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: It is not integrated.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: What we are asking for is a full integration where you go to one place,

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: You make your reports, you submit your documentation and evidence, not that you have to have a menagerie of documents and, you know, investigative lenses to figure out how to navigate the two things.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So administration, you're on your way.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés

chapters.summary: Camarda says Reinvent Albany supports the Citizen Air Complaint Program as a creative enforcement tool. He opposes Intro 561-A because its exemptions would create loopholes and opposes Intro 11 because higher fines could increase delinquency and discourage complainants.
chapters.title: Alex Camarda of Reinvent Albany opposes Intros 561-A and 11

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: My name is Alex Camarda.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I'm a senior policy advisor for Reinvent Albany, a government watchdog group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Reinvent Albany supports the Civilians Air Complaint Program, believing it's a creative, innovative way to leverage civic-minded New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: To extend the compliance reach of the Department of Environmental Protection to enforce laws against idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We're concerned by the bills before the committee today, in particular 561A and Intro 11, both of which we oppose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We oppose 561A because it creates numerous loopholes that will result in more idling, more air pollution, more asthma, and more related diseases like cancer and heart disease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: These loopholes include diesel regeneration, enabling buses to idle anywhere along their routes, enabling buses to idle for 30 minutes without clear beginning and end points,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: allowing vehicles to idle due to undefined mechanical problems, allowing vehicles that have auxiliary battery-powered units in good working condition, which is undefined, to also idle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: More importantly, these loopholes will make it difficult for both complainants and the DEP to discern between an exception to the idling law and improper

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: DEP and complainants, I'm sorry, I already mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We also oppose intro number 11 because we think that increasing the fines is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We think the current fine levels are changing behavior already, and idling has been greatly reduced in many neighborhoods across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We also think that it will increase delinquency on the part of respondents, the commercial vehicle companies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: What we see for fines above $1,000 currently is that the delinquency rates are 60% or higher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: So that will cause complainants to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Not participate because they will not be paid their incentive because the companies won't be paying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro asks whether opponents think 561-A can be amended or should be abandoned. Camarda says he does not think it is fixable and urges the Council to focus on due process, faster hearings, and more resources for DEP and OATH.
chapters.title: Gennaro asks Camarda whether 561-A can be fixed

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And as people testify, it would be important, and I think you were pretty clear that

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And in a way, your testimony touched on that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But to the extent that people can be...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Explicit and say, you know, the current paradigm works, we like it, and we don't want it touched.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's perfectly fine testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so, and, you know, to the extent that you have testimony that you want to submit after the fact about

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
