utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And again, I'm not talking just to you, but to everyone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're trying to make this as constructive a debate.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: possible, you know, like we're trying to get 561 to work.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you think it can never work, that's perfectly acceptable testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And with that said, I'm going to go on to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Did you have to come down from Albany to be here?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Go ahead, let me see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Now, we're based in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We have staff in Albany as well.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Just in response to what you just raised.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I didn't actually ask a question, but I'll tell you what.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'll tell you what.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's just like, you know, I know we're going to have a long hearing, but you're the first witness, so you get the first witness prize.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so why don't you...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Make a comment, you know, in response to what I just said.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I'm asking you a formal question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: In relation to 561A, respectfully, I don't think it's fixable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I think where the council should be focused is on due process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I think there's agreement between the industry and the complainants and environmental groups and civic groups like Rain Van Albany.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: That due process should be expedited.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I think everybody agrees with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Oath and DEP need more resources, as you talked about at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: And I think that's where everyone would agree.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: We want to see complaints processed more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: The industry deserves to get those complaints in a timely manner, and complainants will get paid faster, and you'll see a change in behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Faster for those commercial vehicle companies that are getting complaints for the first time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please.

chapters.summary: Thurston, an NYU School of Medicine air-pollution researcher, describes his work linking PM2.5 to mortality and diesel particles to asthma and heart disease. He warns that regeneration and other exemptions in 561-A could become broad loopholes.
chapters.title: George Thurston links idling pollution to cardiovascular and respiratory harm

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Yeah, George Thurston.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I work at the New York University School of Medicine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I live outside the city, but I commute in and I walk from Grand Central to my office a little over a mile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So I experience the kinds of pollution and probably more noticeable to me because I often carry a pollution monitor, which I recommend, a portable one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And I actually...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we'll let you go on a little bit, but what kind of device do you carry?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Just a portable particulate matter monitor.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Anyway, and I'll present some of those data in my written.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And I study health effects of air pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I published, you mentioned the PM2.5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I published the very first paper relating PM2.5 to mortality in the United States in 1987.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: The US EPA cited my research when they set the standard in 1997.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And I've done studies here in the United States, well, throughout the United States, but in New York City of children's, the backpack study, that was mine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I've done a number of studies in New York showing the continuing effects of this on not just from this particular problem, but from diesel, especially particles in this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And so we need to take vigorous action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So I commend the committee for taking this on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And enforcing these idling rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: However, I also am concerned about the exemptions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: such as for regeneration clean cycles, and could be potential loopholes and should be avoided.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: That's in 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I've done a lot of work with power plants, and they get exemptions something like this, where it says, well, if they change operations, they're allowed to emit for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And you wouldn't believe how many times they call on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It's just, and the emissions of, the annual emissions go way up because they just do it, and they just mark it down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: We just did this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So I think it's really human nature being what it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It doesn't sound like you can find out whether it really was happening or not.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please continue because I held you up for a couple of moments with your other thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So just in conclusion, I think that we need to be more proactive in enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: You know, and you mentioned hiring some new people, maybe more of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And I also think looking at solutions, not just these kind of extreme events, you know, of idling, but it's a general problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: We're bathed in pollution from traffic every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: We walk around.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And if you compare where I live out in Westchester, when I come into work, that's where I get all my exposure to pollution every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So we need to do things like giving incentives for EV trucks, heavy-duty trucks, and to drive that switchover off diesels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: We need to get them.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Professor, I'm going to have to, you know, step in because I'll– I'm going to have to step in and, you know, enforce the time limit.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's all I have to say.

chapters.summary: Gennaro thanks Thurston and says his research helped shift understanding from PM10 to PM2.5. He calls Thurston a 'ringer' and says the committee appreciates his work on air pollution health effects.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks Thurston for PM2.5 research

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just really appreciate, you know, all the work you've done on, you know, PM 2.5 because forever it was like PM 10 and then, you know, and then–

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We got smart because of you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, PM 2.5 is a very different animal than PM 10.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we, you know, certainly appreciate all the work that you've done.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, please put the professor on our ringers list because he's a ringer.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's a compliment.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Compliment.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a compliment.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Professor.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please, the next witness, if you could take the microphone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, that's probably the closest one.

chapters.summary: Perkins says 350 NYC has helped pass major city climate laws and opposes 561-A. She argues the city should not retreat from idling enforcement during a climate crisis and points to Local Law 97 and congestion pricing as examples of successful action.
chapters.title: Margaret Perkins of 350 NYC opposes 561-A and urges climate action

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: My name is Margaret Perkins and I'm a member of the Climate Group 350 NYC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And we have been instrumental in the major climate laws that have been passed in this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: We're very proud of them, including Local Law 97.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And they pull back on fossil fuels and buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: I want to say everybody's probably going to say the same thing about the intricacies of this law 561, and we're very much opposed to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: But I think we forget the bigger picture right now, and the bigger picture is that we are in a climate crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And we have seen the summer, the heat, the bushfires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: We have to do everything we can to reduce the pollutants from fossil fuels.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: They are causing a major source of heating of this planet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And New York City has a duty to do everything it can.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And this includes a bill that works in terms of stopping idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: It's a major contribution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Trucks are 80% of the pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: From vehicles and we have to figure it out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: And I just want to say that New York City has figured out a lot of problems already, which James Gennaro has been instrumental in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Local Law 97, everyone said you can't do it, you can't get the buildings to change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: We have already shown that we have reduced emissions from buildings by 5% in the first year where it was made.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: So if people really, and people do want a change, they will do what has to be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: We've done that with congestion pricing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Oh my God, this was going to be the end of the planet, you know, end of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: It's working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Particulate matter is down, vehicles are down, accidents are down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: So I say we can do idling as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: We have the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Margaret Perkins
utterances.text: Expertise and the drive and motivation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your good testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We appreciate you coming back again to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so we do appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Let me get my slips in order here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Lacertoza, please.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lacertosa represents heating-fuel distributors and says fuel-delivery trucks must run engines to operate pumps. He supports 561-A's recognition of pump use and diesel regeneration, backs its due-process reforms, and opposes Intro 11-A until the process is fixed.
chapters.title: Rocco Lacertosa of NYSEC supports 561-A and opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, just speak right into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's hard to hear.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, you got to get it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair DeNiro and members of the Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: My name is Rocco J.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Lacertoza.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: I'm the CEO of the New York State Energy Coalition, or NYSEC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: NYSEC represents liquid heating fuel distributors in the five boroughs of New York City, Lower Westchester, Nassau, and Suffolk counties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Our members are predominantly small and medium-sized, multi-generational businesses that provide an essential service to homes and businesses throughout the region.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: NYSEC supports effective enforcement of New York City's idling laws and does not condone unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: But enforcement must distinguish unnecessary idling from engine operation that is necessary to perform an essential service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: That distinction is particularly important.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Heating fuel delivery trucks must operate pumps to safely and efficiently deliver fuel to homes, apartment buildings, and businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: That is not unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: We strongly support Intro 561A's recognition of pumps used in fuel delivery as a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: legitimate use, and we urge the Council to ensure the final language clearly protects drivers as when engine operation is necessary to complete a fuel delivery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: NYSEC also supports the bill's exemption for required diesel particulate filter regeneration cycles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Drivers should not face an idling violation for operating a vehicle in compliance with environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: We support the broader reforms in Intro 561A, including replacing percentage-based

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: complaint awards with fixed amounts, establishing reasonable enforcement timelines, and ensuring that respondents receive the video and electronic evidence underlying a violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: These reforms will make the program more fair, reliable, and focused on genuine compliance rather than financial incentives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: NICEQ also supports Intro 869A and its safeguards against the fraudulent evidence and other abuse of citizen complaint process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Finally, NICEQ opposes Intro 11A at this time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: The Council should first implement and evaluate the important reforms in Intro 561A before increasing penalties, particularly for the small...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Businesses that make up our membership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Higher penalties should not come before a fair and reliable enforcement process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: NICEQ urges the Council to advance Intros 561A and 869A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Lassitosa.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Always appreciate working with NICEQ and appreciate your continuing involvement in this process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: And if I had more time, I would speak about what our industry has done.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, when I'm done, I'm going to ask questions of the panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: People might have an ability to get another word in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And our final panelists on this panel.

chapters.summary: Resnick says he is a Brooklyn resident and regular participant in the Citizen Air Complaint Program. He says filming idling trucks causes them to shut off, calls Intro 48 a no-brainer, and urges the Council to withdraw 561-A.
chapters.title: Max Resnick supports Intro 48 and calls 561-A unsalvageable

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Max Resnick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Are we good on time?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Cool.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I am...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Brooklyn resident and a participant in the citizen complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I am testifying asking that the council withdraw 561A and support Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I don't think that Intro 561A is resurrectable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: There are too many loopholes and exceptions, and it does not support the air and environment here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I'm also a city park steward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I take care of street trees, and I recently finished my street tree pruning class as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I love having extra tools in my toolkit to help New York City's environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I started participating in this program in 2024, and I submit complaints on an average of 10 to 15 a month.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Not super regularly, but it's not difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: When I'm walking from my home to and from the subway, when I'm visiting friends, eating out, I'm able to see cars, trucks, and buses idling pretty regularly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: And I live near Coney Island Avenue, a major hub of upcoming development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: This summer, for example, lines of dump trucks and construction vehicles would line up a block away from an elementary school playground and idle for hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: When I started filming them, those trucks stopped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: That's why this program works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: When they would see me walking around, these trucks would turn off almost immediately.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: We know that this program as it is, is effective at reducing idling, reducing particulate matter, and we want more New Yorkers to be equipped with those skills to be able to contribute to that program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Intro 48 is a no-brainer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: It expands language access and hopefully empowers more New Yorkers to be able to participate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I look forward to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: a future with cleaner air and feel proud to contribute to that work through this program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Max.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate you being here and being a participant in the program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Expanding your reach of service to pruning trees.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We do appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I have some questions, but I know that my colleague, Harvey Epstein, has questions for this panel.

chapters.summary: Epstein asks how exempting more trucks would improve the environment. Lacertosa says fuel delivery requires the engine to run the pump, but concedes that future technology might allow pumping without idling and that he does not design trucks.
chapters.title: Epstein questions Lacertosa on pump exemptions and cleaner technology

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I recognize Councilmember Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to thank the panel for being here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't remember your name, sir.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's Rocco Lesher.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Of Rocco.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I'd love to hear why you think these exemptions are going to help the environment by exempting more trucks from the law.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Like what environmental advantages do you see we're going to have by that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: First of all, there's no...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You got to use the microphone.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: There is no way to affect the delivery without the truck running, okay, because the engine operates the pump.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So it's just as simple as that, okay?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The regen process is part of what they do now.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'm just saying about the environmental benefits.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I just really wanted to check what environmental benefits you think this bill will have.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just don't think that it helps our industry whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, we're already delivering a much cleaner project, which is what I was starting to say before about having biodiesel and renewable diesel blended with

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: with our heating oil, and we've reduced tons of emissions from New York City's air over the last two decades.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Which is great.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So we're saying we want to reduce emissions in our air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: We keep doing it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: We're going to higher blends.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But when you're saying this bill, you want to create more exemptions in the bill.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: How does that create cleaner air?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: I don't know that it does one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: But all I can tell you is that there is no way to make a delivery without using a pump.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So basically, the current technology doesn't allow a system to operate the pump without the engine being on.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And there's no system available now that allows that to happen?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And you're saying technologies have a path forward on this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: I don't design trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: You don't design trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: It's above my pay grade.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it's possible that technology is out there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And that trucks can move towards that technology.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And that may reduce the environmental consequences as well as the idling issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Because people are only, you're saying they're only idling now is because they have to because they want the pump to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So if there's a technology that was available that allowed them to not idle while the pump was working, you could certainly use it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it doesn't seem like changing the law to allow more idling would make sense, except maybe allowing, figuring out their technology exists to allow the pump to work without idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rocco J. Lacertosa
utterances.text: That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, great.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I've

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This is one of the other panelists.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: The other panelists seem to be not supportive of this bill.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Am I going down?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Like, are we saying that the change in this law would hurt the environmental regulations, hurt the environment, increase particulate matters?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Is that what I hear you all saying?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You're nodding.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You can maybe just articulate that in the mic because we need to have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Well, I think the implementation would not allow the kind of improvement you could get from a proper bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: That the exemptions would undermine it, basically.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So the exemptions in the bill could undermine the whole intent of the law?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And so...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It does seem like with the chair's goal here is to try to make an industry viable, which we all want to do.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We don't want to undermine this industry without undermining the environment at the same time.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So there's got to be some path, which is what I hear people talking about, of maybe changing the way the industry functions, but also without undermining the good goals and all that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Do you want to?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: Yeah, I just think with a number of the exceptions, as I mentioned in my testimony, I feel like they make the program inoperable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: It's more than just increasing idling or increasing pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I don't think complainants, you know, everyday New Yorkers who are filming videos of idling trucks are going to be able to tell if they're doing diesel regeneration or if their auxiliary battery-powered unit is working or if they have a mechanical problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: I'm not even sure what that is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: And I think DEP will similarly struggle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alex Camarda
utterances.text: So I think it makes the program inoperable in addition to increasing pollution.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I do also want to ask the panel, we've heard from written testimony from DEP that they are concerned about the volume of complaints that are coming in and the quality of some of those videos that are being sent in.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We'd love to hear from this panel about additional solutions that might be available to streamline that process.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Obviously, the chair and people in the committee will have the ability to increase funding, but also what other solutions might be available to deal with the quality of the videos coming in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Before the answer comes forward, I just want to tell Councilmember Epstein that, you know, we've got a five-minute clock for council members, which I didn't set, but I certainly want this answer.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I certainly want your question answered.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Chad.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'll be done after this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You bet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: I'm a casual participant in this program and have basically stumbled on ways to be able to submit videos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Most of my videos have been accepted, and I really appreciate the community of other people who are also submitting these videos, who provide guidance and coaching to make sure that the quality is good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Nobody wants to be wasting DEP's time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: We don't want to be submitting false claims.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: We want to be doing good work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: And there's a community of people who have been doing this for years who are very generous with their time and are happy to share best practices and tips and tricks to make this work better.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So making that more publicly available might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Max Resnick
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Thank you, Council Member, for some great questioning.

chapters.summary: Aviles asks Thurston to describe pollution disparities. Thurston says South Bronx and Harlem neighborhoods are surrounded by highways and face much higher diesel exposure, with cardiovascular and respiratory effects extending beyond asthma.
chapters.title: Aviles questions Thurston on PM2.5 disparities in environmental justice communities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And now I recognize Council Member Reveals for questions.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I just had a quick question for the professor.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed your first name.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: George.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: George.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: George, in your study, can you just briefly describe for the record the disparities of PM2.5 in environmental justice communities and more wealthier communities?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Yes, I have done studies, especially in the South Bronx, and we see much higher levels, especially diesel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: I mean, basically, if you're in the South Bronx and you're near one highway, if you move away from it, you're moving towards another highway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It's enveloped by...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Highways all around it in every direction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Harlem's a lot like that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So there's major throughways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And then there's congestion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And congestion pricing is not helping them much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Although we have seen generally lower air pollution levels following the congestion pricing throughout the city with some hotspots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: But anyway, so that and the effects of them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: One of my studies we have one we're looking at right now with cardiovascular damage from local pollution on New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It still continues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: We've documented it before, especially traffic pollution, cardiovascular, respiratory asthma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It's a real problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Diesel particles are an antigen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So they not only have the toxic effects of fossil fuels with metals,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: transition metals that cause oxidative stress, inflammation, which underlies a lot of disease throughout the body, so it has systemic effects.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So we're not just talking about, I mean, asthma is a very big problem, and I'm not dismissing it, but I'm saying it goes beyond that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And every New Yorker, not just people who have respiratory problems, we're all threatened by this, and there are disparities in the levels of exposures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And that's one of the reasons why I think, you know, we're talking about climate, but also health, that, like, the city has great buying power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And they could start buying up these trucks and solving this problem, the solutions, and then creating a market that private people could then buy them and have battery-based operations, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Like, I own a Chevy Volt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: It's like 15 years old, runs like new because it's electric most of the time, and then occasionally it's got a backup engine that once in a blue moon I need it if I'm going to travel to the airport or something.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: And so, you know, you can design trucks like that, and I think there are trucks like that, where they have a battery pack for around the town and then an engine that will occasionally back it up so there's no, you know, running out of power and plugging it in and waiting for it to charge up kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: So there's technology solutions, and we should be driving those.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I couldn't agree with you more, and it means that our city needs to use all the tools in the toolbox, including translating

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: and allowing for documents to be submitted, particularly complaints to be submitted in languages other than English,

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: which the administration has not solved because the instructions are all questions are required to be answered in English.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So just for the record, that is one thing we can certainly do, but we have,

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I agree with you wholeheartedly, our city needs to use its market power, its enforcement power, and every other regulatory option to make sure that it's...

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: communities are protected, and particularly environmental justice communities who have bore the brunt of infrastructure that the rest of the city also benefits from.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: This is a public health issue and an urgent one.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro thanks the panel and then recognizes longtime environmental advocate Eric Goldstein of NRDC in the audience. He calls Goldstein a friend, mentor, and colleague before moving to the next panel.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks first panel and recognizes Eric Goldstein

utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'd like to thank this panel for its great addition to the discourse here, and we really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We look forward to staying in touch.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Any further information you want to transfer to the committee, you know how to do that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so thank you all very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Thurston
utterances.text: Thanks for listening.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, sure thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And before I call the next panel, I'm just going to embarrass my longtime friend, Eric Goldstein of NRDC, who has graciously joined us.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We go back a long way, friend, mentor, colleague, and great to see you, Eric.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Are you embarrassed yet, or should I keep going?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's enough.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, good.

chapters.title: Gennaro calls industry panel on idling bills

utterances.text: I have David, I can't make out the last name, from the Interior Demolition Contractors Association.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, great, as long as you got up there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Joseph Ferrara, Aggregate and Cement Trucking, LLC.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Melissa Barbour from the Mechanical Contractors Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the last one, I mean, I don't, as you know, I don't set the panels, but Rocco got put in with the environmentalists, so he's got some environmental cred now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So we have testimony from Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do we have any other written testimony?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Any other panels?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Witnesses?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Felice has testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And.

utterances.text: This time I'm going to go from my left to my right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So, sir, you're up.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know I called your name, but I don't know which one you are.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So just, sure, just begin your good testimony with the sergeant's prompting and state your name for the record.

chapters.summary: Ferrara describes his family cement-delivery business and says it receives many citizen complaints. He argues the program has become a 'money grab' and suggests complainants should first tell drivers to shut off engines rather than immediately filming them.
chapters.title: Joseph Ferrara says cement trucking is inundated by citizen idling complaints

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairman Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: My name is Joseph Ferrara, and I am an owner and president of Aggregate and Cement Trucking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: My son and I own and operate this company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Prior to this, my family was in the ready mix concrete business for our brothers building materials from 1969 through 2015.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So our business involves delivering cement, which is a raw material as opposed to concrete, to concrete plants and construction sites.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So we go to the same locations every day, multiple deliveries, and we are just getting inundated with these idling violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: And my question to the enforcement community and the legislators is,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: This is, we're in favor of eliminating or minimizing unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: We're all for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: I just, I have two grandchildren.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: I'd love to see them live and healthy long lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: But if the objective of this legislation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: is to minimize or eliminate unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Most of our violations come from citizen complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: We don't have an opportunity to cross-examine them, but they take a video, and it's kind of like, gotcha, and it's a money grab.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So my suggestion...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Is if a citizen is going to take a video, if they want to eliminate unnecessary idling, we have 18 truck drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: They make dozens of deliveries a day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: I've instructed them on the law, and you shouldn't idle if you're not pumping off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: But have the citizen tell the driver, hey, do you know you can't do that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: And if they say F you and they take a video of it, but if they stop, they've accomplished their purpose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Someone on the prior panel talked about how the drivers shut their trucks off when they see them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: But couldn't we make it a requirement if you really want to clean up the air?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Instructor drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: They may not

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: That's the purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: This has become a multi-million dollar money grab.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: And it's not fair to businesses that pay taxes, employ union members.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says the committee asks the questions but that he is trying to make the program fairer. He notes that environmental advocates are criticizing his bill, which he says shows the committee is trying to balance competing concerns.
chapters.title: Gennaro responds to Ferrara on balancing enforcement and business concerns

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm going to have to...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, it was a two-minute limit, and I wanted to give you a little latitude on that, which I did.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I was happy to do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I appreciate your question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, we don't answer questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But I...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I think the good people who are in the part of the anti-idling crusade,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: you hear what they're saying about me and my bill.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so I'm trying to do everything I can.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: To make it fair.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And if they were lauding me and telling me how much of a great guy I was,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I think the fact that they're not is evidence of me and this committee and this council trying to bring this process

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: somehow make it fair and better and workable for everyone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, we wouldn't be here

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: today if I wasn't looking to make changes to the program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I appreciate your being here today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We look forward to working with you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And with that, I'm going to go on to the next witness, and members may have questions for you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And okay, so that was, wait a minute, wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So that was Joseph Ferrara.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And you are who?

chapters.summary: Atkin represents unionized interior demolition contractors and says their trucks are required to be certified clean idle. He asks for an exemption when trucks must run engines at commercial buildings to wait for debris containers, similar to California's clean-idle rules.
chapters.title: David Atkin seeks clean-idle exemption for interior demolition trucks

utterances.text: David Atkin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin

utterances.text: We appreciate you being here today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wait for the sergeant's prompt and begin with your good testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
