utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: The Interior Demolition Contractors Association.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, talk right into the mic.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Make sure the light is on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: The Interior Demolition Contractors Association.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: A little louder, a little louder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay, is it not for profit?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Speak like a contractor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: I'm an attorney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: It's not for profit.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wait, I'm a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I meant lawyers on that side.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: It's a not-for-profit trade association that represents unionized interior demolition contractors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Our members are generally family-owned small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: They perform interior demolition work within commercial buildings and carding work for commercial clients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Our members provide middle-class jobs for our workers because they're union.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Our members use certified clean idle trucks for all of our pickups.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Our trucks are regulated by the New York City Business Integrity Commission, where it's mandated we...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: purchase or upgrade our trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Those upgrades are extraordinarily expensive to our small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: As a point of reference, the Certified Clean Idle Program was first introduced in the state of California.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We thank everybody for their efforts with regard to updating the idling law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We agree with many of those efforts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We do need to raise some issues that are unique to our industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: When our members operate at a commercial building, they face particular hardships.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: First, we pick up the debris when the building owners allow us to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: This is up to them, not us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: That is generally on off hours when there is little or no pedestrian traffic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: The debris is loaded into containers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Second, we must wait for the loaded containers to come down to the loading dock or to the curb.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Those containers use the building's elevators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We cannot continuously shut down our engines between loads.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We just can't do it because the time, if you shut your truck down, it takes time to regenerate and get up to full power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: You just cannot do that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please continue for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I was playing with you before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: So we're asking for an exemption.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Which is similar to what the state of California has, for certified clean idle trucks, for when you're at a commercial building, that you have an exemption for when you're doing what we do, which is interior work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And we would say that, as the state of California says, when you're near...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: a facility like a school, of course that exemption should not apply, and there are going to be multiple tickets going to be issued.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says he will return to Atkin with a question about certified clean idle and calls Felice Farber next. He notes her long history with the committee and asks her to begin when the sergeant prompts her.
chapters.title: Gennaro moves panel to Felice Farber

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, we're going to have to go to Felice, but I'm going to come back to you with a question about the certified clean idol.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Remind me to ask you that, okay?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Uh-oh.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No stranger to this committee or to this council.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I had you slip right here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As if I need to slip to know who you are.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I've known you forever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so thank you, Felice Farber, for being here on behalf of the...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Now, are you still working with Liz?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Are you guys?

chapters.summary: Farber represents union specialty trade contractors and says running engines often powers pumps, lifts, decontamination units, or emissions cycles. She supports 561-A with additional amendments but asks the Council to hold Intro 11-A until the process is fixed.
chapters.title: Felice Farber of STA supports 561-A with amendments and opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: So the Subcontractors Trade Association is a member of the Building Trade Employers Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: They're an association of 24 different trade associations, of which we're a member of them.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So that's the connection.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I got that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for being here, of course.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Nice to see you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And please commence with your good testimony when the sergeant prompts you to do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: So the subcontractor, I'm Felice Farber, Executive Director of the Subcontractors Trade Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: We represent more than 350 union specialty trade contractors, including electrical, plumbing, sheet metal, demolition, concrete pumping, remediation, and many more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Their crews and trucks are on job sites in every borough, every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: We want cleaner air and less needless idling, too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: The citizens'air complaint...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: program as it operates now is generating penalties without changing much on the street and is not addressing the problems in environmental justice communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: On a construction job, a running engine is often doing work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: It may be powering a pump, a lift gate, or an environmental decontamination unit that keeps workers safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: It may be running equipment for street and utility work in the roadway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: It may be finishing an emissions control cycle the law requires or keeping a driver safe in dangerous heat or cold while waiting to get onto a job site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Our members are being ticketed in exactly these situations, even when the truck displays a valid exemption sticker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Timing makes it worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Notices arrive many months after the fact, and hearings come a year later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: By then, no one can piece together what happened at a single stop, and evidence that would clear a contractor is too often not considered, and opportunities to take corrective action against that driver are not available.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Intro 561 takes steps to fix this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: We support it with additional amendments, which are outlined in our detailed written testimony provided, and in the specific recommendations that are put forth in the BTA's testimony that they'll be providing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: We further ask the committee to hold on Intro 11A, raising the fines and escalating them across an entire company rather than by vehicle or driver, punishes small and mid-sized businesses before the process itself is fixed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: We urge you to fix the system first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Farber.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We certainly appreciate working with you and getting the benefit of your perspective.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm going to have a question for you, too, I think, when we finish the panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Melissa Barber.

chapters.summary: Barber says mechanical contractors' trucks often idle for boom lifts, no-heat calls, or job-site waiting. She argues delayed notices and hearings make defense impossible, supports 561-A and related bills with amendments, and opposes 11-A's fleet-wide penalty increases.
chapters.title: Melissa Barber of MCA supports 561-A, 562, and 869-A but opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: That's me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Hi, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro and Council Member Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: I'm Melissa Barber, Assistant Director of the Mechanical Contractors Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Our contractors install and service heating, cooling, refrigeration, and fire sprinkler systems across the five boroughs, employing members of Steamfitters Local 638.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: We also share the council's goal of reducing unnecessary idling, but the program right now as it works today is not meeting that goal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Instead, it's burying our small businesses in fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Our members'trucks make many stops a day, mostly with their engines off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: When an engine is running, there's usually a reason.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: It might be powering a boom or lift gate, answering a no-heat call in extreme weather, or waiting in line to deliver to an active job site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: If violations are now arriving six to 12 months later, hearings can take 15 months or more, and a fine that shows up a year later does nothing to change what a driver does on the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: It only punishes a company that cannot reconstruct one stop out of hundreds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Enforcement also isn't reaching the neighborhoods that need it most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: PP's own commissioner stated that complaints are concentrated in the Manhattan core, wealthier parts of Brooklyn and Western Queens, and that there's minimal attention to the areas that need it most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: That's why we support Intro 561A, 562, and 869A with amendments and ask that Intro 11AB held.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: As written, 11A would raise fines to as much as $3,000 and escalate them across an entire fleet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: That penalizes a company's size rather than its idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: We have submitted detailed recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: We support the recommendations also developed by the BTEI and the STA for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: We want a program that's accurate, timely, and fair, and we welcome a chance to work with you on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro asks when vehicles are required to have diesel particulate filters and how an observer can tell whether regeneration is occurring. Atkin, Farber, and Ferrara describe clean-idle requirements, dashboard lights, and regeneration cycles.
chapters.title: Gennaro questions industry panel on diesel particulate filters and regeneration

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I want to make sure that I have your...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Written to this is you this this oh yeah this is you okay um okay thank you thank you and then i have some council is prompting me to ask

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: questions what's well the whole panel

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, this is to tout le monde, everybody.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, question one.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Under what circumstances are your vehicles required by law to be equipped with a diesel particulate filter?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, you know, like you don't have to.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, not everyone has to answer every question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Could you put on the thing?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm not hearing you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Our entire fleet is required to have it because of the fact that we are regulated by BIC, and they require us to be certified clean aisle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: So when we regenerate, what happens is a light comes on on the truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: The driver stops where he can and it's going to be regeneration.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, for those who are not sort of facile with regeneration, that includes people who are watching online or whatever, people sit up, watch council hearings.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I don't know, but they do.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you could go through that technology a little bit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Generations to eliminate the buildup within the system, which requires it to be burned off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: So that is required by the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Apparatus that's on the truck, which is...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Is that like a trap oxidizer or something?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Is it a similar technology?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: But the reality is that we, at times, do get tickets for regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: So there was an oath decision in which the Salvation Army...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Had a truck that was regenerating and it got a ticket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Regeneration is required to be undergone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: If it's not, the truck itself could be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And it's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: We want them to stop, not immediately, but as soon as they can, in a reasonable place so that they undergo regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And that is helpful for both the environment, ultimately, as well as for everything with regard to this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And that's very important.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, let's come back to the original question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Same question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Under what circumstances are your vehicles required by law to be equipped with a diesel particulate filter, which is a little different technology than what you just were talking about, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, well, then help me out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Help me out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Help me out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: This was a mandate by the New York City Business Integrity Commission, and I believe it was part of a city council law as well that required

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: all these vehicles to be upgraded with their newest engines, I think they were Tier 4 engines, and to have certified clean idle vehicles as the version of that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Farrar, do you have anything to add to that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Well, in the concrete industry, DEP came out with the regulations or specs in their contracts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So most public agencies have that to deliver materials to a job site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: You have to have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: And basically, if it's a city contract, if it's a city contract, city, state, most most contracts have those provisions and a region.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Basically, it superheats the exhaust to burn the soot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So the soot doesn't actually get in the atmosphere.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So it's like thermally destroyed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: When the truck is running, going back and forth, it's no problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: But when it's idle and it's making delivery to a job site, that's when it generates the need to regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: So that you're not generating diesel particulate filters.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Second question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Second question.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: How could an observer determine whether a vehicle is engaging in a regeneration clean cycle for a diesel particulate filter?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Are there visual signs, smells, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And is there any kind of like signage on the truck that indicates anything?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But that's just my addition to that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But the question is, how can an observer determine whether a vehicle is engaging in a regeneration clean cycle for a diesel particulate filter?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Are there visual signs, smells, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: How do you tell?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: That's where if the conversation was held between the driver and the citizen, there's a monitor inside the cab of the truck that shows the regeneration process is in effect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So you could see, but it's inside the cab.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, but the advocates who are participating in this program don't think the regeneration thing should even exist, so they're not going to ask you about it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be real here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: In addition, if you had timely notice of the violation so that you could look it up, you could provide evidence showing, you know, documentation showing that the vehicle was going through that regeneration cycle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But if you get the thing 18 months later, you know, yeah, it's gone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: And at Oath, they disregard any information like that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: At oath, they disregard what?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: Evidence that you were not idling or in a legitimate operation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: So we have one example where one of our members, and this is not a diesel clean idle vehicle, but they have evidence that the vehicle was in fact not running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: And they could tell by how the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: The video and that was not relevant because you had to bring the manual for the vehicle operation with you to show that if there were no rear lights on that the vehicle wasn't idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: But the challenge is really the timeliness of getting the information so that you can mount a defense and take corrective action because if someone is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Felice Farber
utterances.text: parked on Queens Boulevard, you know, scrolling through their phone, they shouldn't be idling and you should be in a position to take corrective action to notify your driver that that's not a permissible activity.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Farrar, it looks like you're about to...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, okay.

chapters.summary: Epstein challenges Ferrara's suggestion that residents knock on truck windows and asks about regeneration timing. Panelists say regeneration can take 15 to 20 minutes and that drivers pull over when a dashboard light signals the need.
chapters.title: Epstein questions industry panel on truck confrontations and regeneration timing

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I recognize Councilmember Epstein for questions of this panel.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to thank this panel.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Do people really think on this panel that a human being who's concerned about idling should knock on the– you actually think too much to knock on the window of the truck and say, hey, you're idling and that violates the law.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Can you turn off your car?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You think that is a realistic solution here?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Well, I just last week got a citizen's complaint from a truck that was idling in March of 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: It just came last Friday.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: And when I looked at the video, after the three minutes were up, the citizen went to the driver and was asking him questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: How many tons are you pumping off?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So if they could have that conversation and the objective is to reduce or minimize unnecessary idling, they could have that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: So we only have a couple minutes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So the answer is you think yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You think it's a healthy thing for someone to go knock on the truck and say, hey, you're idling.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Can you stop?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: That's what you think is the solution here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: It's having a civil conversation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But do you think the driver.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Communication solves all problems.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Do you think the driver would, that would result in a civil conversation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Well, if they have their video camera on, my driver.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: was disrespectful in any way, that I would pay the fine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: I'll make sure question.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: How would they contact you if your driver was being uncivil?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Like, what would be the goal?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Like, you think they should just send an email to you notifying you that the driver was being uncivil?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Like, somehow contact the business connected to the driver?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: They could, but all I'm just...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I mean, I'm just, let's be realistic.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This is New York, right?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I mean, we all want to be civil.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We all want to be respectful.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But I've actually, in front of my building, you know, for the last, you know, decades I've been living there, said to someone, hey, you're idling in front of my building.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It's right next to a school playground.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Do you mind stopping?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I've been cursed at more than one time for doing just that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: At the same time, I've been civil to people who take their dog and put them on the swings and the playground equipment and say, hey, this is like my kids play here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Don't do that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And they are uncivil back.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I don't think our goal is to put people into difficult situations.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Our goal is to try to reduce particulates in the air, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So I just want to be clear just to make sure that this regeneration, can that happen when the vehicle's actively being used, like driving around?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So you can do regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You don't have to idle to regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You can regenerate while the vehicle is moving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: You have, when...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Talk right into it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: When you, when that light goes on, you have to pull back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: When that light goes on.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: The regeneration light, you're saying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: You have to pull over within a very short period of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And that's when you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Do the regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: You're not driving when you regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So regeneration only happens when you're not moving, and that's the technology that exists today?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And how long does that regeneration take?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Could you find out and get back to us about how long that regeneration takes?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joseph Ferrara
utterances.text: It's about 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So basically, whenever that happens, you're going to have to pull over wherever you are and regenerate for 15 to 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Within a reasonable location.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: When that light goes on, the driver is told to pull over, not immediately, but within a reasonable time period.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: Because you have to stop this vehicle, else it's going to destroy the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: And so you pull over where you find a place which is an appropriate place to just stop and let it regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - David Atkin
utterances.text: That's what you do.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I just want to, I know you mentioned the issue of like fines being centered in Manhattan and Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: He's saying that.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: More of these should be happening in other parts of the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: I'm just saying the DEP's own testimony at the last hearing was that the fines were concentrated in those areas and not in the areas that...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: could benefit from cleaner air.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So just so I'm clear, you're saying areas of Manhattan won't benefit by cleaner air?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: No, of course they will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: But I do think that it's easy bait for a citizen to use the most densely populated areas to try to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: capitalize on the program.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And so the densely populated areas, which have a lot of trucks and a lot of humans, are the ones that have a higher particulate matter, too, because they have less trees.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: The DEP said it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Well, I mean, in my district, which is Manhattan, which is also a residential part of the city, also has a lot of high particulate matters, especially with the FDR that's in my district.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We have a lot of truck traffic in my district.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And so we see a lot of pollution and we want to reduce those that behavior, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: That makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So creating more exceptions to idling, I don't think would incentivize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Melissa Barber
utterances.text: Actually, in my more complete testimony, I simply said that I thought that you should base fines on the areas where there's the most air pollution versus necessarily concentrating them in one area.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

chapters.summary: Goldstein calls the citizen complaint provision one of the Council's most innovative environmental laws. NRDC supports Intros 11-A, 48, 562, and 869-A, but Goldstein says 561-A needs additional work and does not support it in its current form.
chapters.title: Eric Goldstein of NRDC supports most bills but says 561-A needs work

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Cut it out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm supposed to say your name.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: I'm Eric Goldstein from the Natural Resources Defense Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Thank you for your leadership on this and so many other environmental issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: The citizen complaint enforcement provision of the New York City Air Code was one of the most innovative environmental laws ever passed by the city council and a good example of the council's national leadership on environmental issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Indeed, NRDC filed one of the earliest citizen complaint enforcement actions more than 30 years ago when we chased after

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: express buses spewing black smoke along Madison Avenue and successfully were able to convince DEP to enforce action against them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: NRDC supports intros 11A, 48, 562, and 869A, all of which enhance the program's operations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: But there is a need for additional reforms to the citizen enforcement program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: One challenge is that in recent years, citizen activists have filed so many complaints

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: that this single section of law has placed an enormous burden on DEP staff and hampered the agency from undertaking other environmental enforcement actions that may be equal to or even higher priorities for the Mandami administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Second problem is that, at least historically, citizen complaint filings have not sufficiently targeted environmental justice communities where air pollution levels have been their highest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: And perhaps the biggest problem of the existing scheme is that it simply is not, in too many instances, had the desired effect of changing behavior and stopping pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: For too many violators of this law, they continue to treat the statute and the fines simply as a cost of doing business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: That's why one concept in Intro 561A that we strongly support would provide an incentive for vehicle operators to install less polluting equipment,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: although we believe this provision needs further strengthening so that it will accomplish the objectives you are seeking to achieve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Intro 561A attempts to address some of these issues but needs additional work.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please finish your thoughts because I gave you a hard time before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: I will just say that while we do not support Intro 561A in its current form, we look forward to working with you to digesting all of the good testimony you've heard today and to coming up with legislation that will enhance this very important program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Eric.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, we have to hear it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We have to get it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: input if we're going to get to where we need to be.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I appreciate your ongoing partnership on this and countless other occasions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So thank you again for being here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Is Mendez, right?

chapters.summary: Mendez says NYLPI works on environmental justice and clean air in communities burdened by transportation pollution. She asks the Council to pass Intros 11 and 48 and reject 561-A because its broad exemptions would weaken enforcement.
chapters.title: Suhali Mendez of NYLPI urges passage of 11 and 48 and rejection of 561-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Yes, hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro and Councilmember Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: My name is Suhali Mendez, and I'm the Policy and Legislative Coordinator at New York Lawyers for the Public Interest, which I'll reference as NOPI from going forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: NOPI has three requests from the council today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: That is to pass Intro 11 to strengthen penalties and enforcement against repeat violators, pass Intro 48 to expand language access and participation in the Citizens Air Complaint Program,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: and reject the current iteration of Intro 561A because of its broad exemptions would undermine the enforcement and effectively weaken one of the city's most successful anti-pollution programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: NOPE works to advance environmental justice and clean air in communities that bear disproportionate burden of the transportation pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And as someone who was born as well as raised in the Bronx, I've seen firsthand how vehicle emissions affect communities like mine, where residents live, work, and attend school near highways, truck routes, and bus depots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Through our advocacy and research on school bus pollution, we have done...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Oh, wow.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I have a soft spot for New York always.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: We appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: We've documented real harm caused by excessive idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Illegal idling is not just a quality of life issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: It is a public health and environmental justice issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And that is why NOPE supports Intro 11 and Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Together, these bills will strengthen enforcement, increase accountability, as well as expand access to communities that are often the most impacted by transportation-related air pollution.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I think I'm going to have to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, I got a soft spot, but it's not Jell-O, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I respect that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: I will summarize by saying we urge the council to strengthen and weaken New York City's anti-idling laws by passing Intros 11 and 48 and rejecting 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: Before polluter convenience and environmental justice deserves stronger protections, not weaker ones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Suhali Méndez
utterances.text: And I thank you for your time and consideration.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says he wants to work collaboratively with NRDC and NYLPI and invites them to offer legal language. He says something must be done about 561-A because the status quo is not working optimally.
chapters.title: Gennaro invites environmental lawyers to help draft 561-A language

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And to both witnesses, the first two, you know, you've been doing legislation for a long time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, we...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Have to do something with 561, we got it, something has to happen because like the status quo is, you know, not really working in an optimum way and that's what we're trying to achieve.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
