utterances.text: It's just like, there's nothing wrong with that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we want to hear from people that care about the environment, they care about, you know, pollution.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, we're not snobs about getting input on

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is how we would do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is how New York lawyers would do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And our D.C.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Would do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we look forward to further discussions on how we can sort of forge that partnership.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So we're a team right now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So you're conscripted.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Ryan, correct?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Now, you just get the microphone nice and close.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You got to put the button on.

chapters.summary: Scott-Loki says he is a former delivery driver and environmental consultant who has submitted thousands of complaints. He opposes Intros 11-A, 561-A, 562, and 869-A, and says the diesel regeneration exemption would be nearly impossible to verify.
chapters.title: Ryan Scott-Loki opposes 561-A and disputes regeneration claims

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: How's that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairman Gennaro and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: My name is Ryan Scott-Loki.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I'm a former delivery driver with more than 17 years of firsthand experience in the operation and management of commercial motor vehicle fleets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Today, I work as an environmental consultant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I help small businesses understand city, state, and federal environmental regulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Learn how to comply with these regulations, and how to resolve outstanding violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I am also an active and regular participant in the city's civilian air, noise, and sanitation enforcement programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I have submitted and documented over 5,000 complaints in my experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: These experiences give me a unique perspective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I see firsthand how these enforcement programs affect the small businesses, commercial drivers, civilian enforcers, and the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Based on that experience, I oppose Intros 11A, 561A, 562, and 869A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I support Intros 48 and Resolution T2026-2662.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I did want to speak about Intro 11A, but we're very limited on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: So let me just focus on 561A and most importantly, the regeneration arguments made by the prior panel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: For starters, in 561A, the most problematic provision proposed is the proposed exemption for diesel vehicles undergoing diesel particulate filter regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: That's also known as a DPF regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: The statements of fact, or sorry, the misstatements of fact in the last panel are abhorrent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I assume the provision is well-intentioned, but it's simply unworkable in reality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: With my extensive experience, over 17 years of firsthand experience, I can only estimate whether a diesel vehicle is undergoing regeneration while outside the vehicle at maybe a 70% accuracy rate,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: at least while observing it outside the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: The smaller and newer the vehicle, the more difficult that determination becomes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: If someone with my level of experience cannot reliably identify regeneration from outside a vehicle, I have no idea how we could reasonably inspect an oath hearing officer who may have little or no comparable experience with diesel engines to make that determination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I'm happy to answer questions on how the actual process for generation works, but vehicles are absolutely able to regenerate in both an active and a passive method.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: They do not have to pull over in most cases to be able to regenerate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: They are able to continue doing it while they drive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: The statement that they have to pull over because there's a magical light or something like that is asinine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: It is true that vehicles and diesel vehicles may have to have regeneration done at a particular time, but not in the manner that they described.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, you made that point.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate you being here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate all of your years of experience and the experience that you bring to bear on this panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: With that, I'll...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Both witnesses.

chapters.summary: A resident holding a baby says the Citizen Air Complaint Program has reduced Con Edison idling in his eastern Queens neighborhood. He opposes 561-A and describes receiving a death threat years earlier for prosecuting noise complaints.
chapters.title: Parent with baby testifies on cleaner air in eastern Queens

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's the baby's name?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Oh, I promised I wasn't going to make a spectacle of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Can I just keep her private?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I just...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You can meet her.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, no, because, yeah, then it'd be on the record.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: People would see it, you know, and whatever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I get it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But she is a...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You can start now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: She is a bit of a witness to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: To the fact that the CACP has made a difference, at least where I live in Eastern Queens, where I'm probably among the only participants in the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Whereas a few years ago, Con Ed would be on all the time, and if I was walking around the neighborhood before I knew about the program, I'd be like, oh, I gotta cross the street to avoid, you know, the stinky fumes, because I really don't like the stinky fumes, and I don't like the noise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And she doesn't like loud mechanical noises either.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Now they're off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And if the Consolidated Edison Company can do this, if they can be resilient, I mean, this one, it was her first time on the subway today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I think she's being very resilient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I don't understand why so many companies here can't modify their behavior accordingly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: They want us to adapt our laws to them as opposed to them adapting to, you know, the market of the, you know, the greatest city in the world.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But really has made a difference and we can walk right past them and she's not bothered at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I'm also a bit sensitive to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: to know

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And so I wanted to bring something to your attention that I don't think anyone else will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I used to prosecute some noise hearings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I really do not like when ice cream trucks just sit at a corner and you can hear them for blocks away and they're just on and on and on and the city wouldn't do anything about it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I prosecuted a modest number of these complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I received a death threat in the mail for my efforts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And so, you know, I hear, oh, you should come up to the truck and tell us to turn off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I don't appreciate.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Address the, you know, address the council, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Yeah, so, you know, I don't think that's fair for anyone to have to experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And DEP is trying to outsource.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: A lot more of their efforts to us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And that's what this would do with the specific timeline saying, okay, well, your work is either going to go down the toilet or you're going to have to put your name out there and be exposed to this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I really don't think that's fair to anybody.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, I certainly appreciate the personal testimony that you bring to bear as a resident, as a father, as someone who's trying to make a better world for his child.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And your testimony is very impactful.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And you have participated in the program, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And it bore dividends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I'm grateful for our walks that are quieter and cleaner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And I think.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, regarding, and it sounds like you live in Councilmember Lee's district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so, you know, we, back when I did the noise code in 2005, you know, we came to a grand compromise on the ice cream trucks.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: They could only sound their bells when they're moving.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: When they stop, they have to shut them off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Kids have ice cream radar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: They know the truck is there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just saying, but it is currently illegal.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We don't have to legislate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's been done.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, no, no.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So now it's on the enforcement side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Because the city refused it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: In fact, my local city council office, they call me the Grinch because I actually didn't force it, which I'm perfectly fine with.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But as a result of that, you know, I got an anonymous death threat in the mail.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: From the Mrs.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Softy guy?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It was anonymous, so I'm not going to impugn anybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But it's very likely the case because I can explain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So that's a saga you should work out with Councilmember Lee, who was very responsive.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm sorry that that happened.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's terrifying.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's terrifying.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: They're much better now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: If we go to a party in Nassau County, again, that made a huge improvement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So both the noise, I mean, I don't participate in that anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But there's a little less of a need because an impact was had beforehand.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: But I don't like, this would require us to do more and get less in return.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And in tech terms, if you want to add a new term that's I'm sure never been used at a hearing here before, in shitification, that's what would be happening.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Put that on the list.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: So in my view, 561A is irreconcilable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Irreconcilable for a bunch of reasons.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for your passionate testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Jonathan Gorin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Jonathan Gorin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Gorin, who has asthma, says he will address claims that trucks are ticketed while using equipment. He reads the existing air-code exemption for loading, unloading, or processing devices, including lifts, cranes, pumps, drills, hoists, and mixers.
chapters.title: Jonathan Gorin reads processing-device exemption from air code

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: My name is Jonathan Gorin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: I live in New York and I have asthma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: So this directly impacts me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: I do too.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: I had something written up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: However, I'm going to ditch that and address some of the claims I heard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Most prominently that I heard that vehicles are receiving tickets when they were engaged in

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: an active processing, like when the vehicle was pumping or using a crane, I heard that they were getting tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: I want to take the time to remind the committee what the law is right now and why that's not true.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: So reading directly from

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Reading directly from the law, section, the code, section 24-163, operation of a motor vehicle, A, no person shall cause or permit the engine of a motor vehicle

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: other than a legally authorized motor vehicle to idle for longer than three minutes, dot, dot, dot, excuse me, except as in provided as subdivision F in the section while, um,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: parking, then it defines, like, it gives some more details, dot, dot, dot, and then it gives exemptions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: The exemptions are, unless the engine is used to operate a loading, unloading, or processing device.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: So your next question is, what's a processing device?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Well, luckily, that's defined in the rules, title, I believe, title,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: 15, section 3901, processing device.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: For the purposes of section 24-163 of the admin code, the term processing device shall mean a,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: excuse me, one, a device that accomplishes the function for which the vehicle or equipment was designed other than transporting goods or people via a mechanical connection to the engine, including, but not limited to, operating a lift, crane,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: pump, drill, hoist, or mixer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: I'm going to leave my testimony at that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Gorin
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We are familiar with the law, but we appreciate, you know, you had...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Getting that in-depth knowledge of the law and, you know, calling out what you think needs to be called out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We certainly appreciate your patience and your willingness to be here to give you good testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And that goes for the entire panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I have no, I personally, Harvey, you got anything for this panel?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I do, Jim, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Good, thanks.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so set it at five minutes.

chapters.summary: Epstein asks whether witnesses agree businesses should be notified sooner, and all do. Scott-Loki explains active versus passive diesel regeneration and warns that a regeneration exemption would create an unrebuttable defense.
chapters.title: Epstein questions panel on notice timing and active versus passive regeneration

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Eric, you mentioned that you were open to some...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Changes to 561A to improve what processing of these complaints or?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Well, one thing that we believe needs to be enhanced is the timing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: So you want to provide

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: I had sufficient time for...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Timing for when people get notified of them?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: So, I mean, there are a number of small fixes that can improve this, which is, I think, what most of us are after.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, basically.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it sounds like we want businesses to know because that's how you change behavior.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: If you wait a year, the driver might be gone.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You want them to have quick notice of this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So they can try to change behavior, but not change the underlying idling law.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Is that what I heard you saying?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Goldstein
utterances.text: That certainly is one of the elements that we think should be addressed.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So does anybody disagree on this panel that we should notify the businesses sooner that there's a violation?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We can say it orally so we can, it's on the record.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: They should be notified earlier.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We all agree they should be notified earlier, which is great.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it sounds like we agree they should be notified earlier on that there are existing exemptions within the law for when they're doing their work.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Is that what I heard you say?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: If they're actively doing something, regeneration obviously is a different conversation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: It sounds like you have really specific knowledge about how regeneration works, and what we heard from the last panel may not be exactly the way you understand it, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Would you like to expound?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, could you please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: So essentially the last panel failed to mention the fact that there is a difference between active and passive regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Active is the actual activity when you would pull over and you would quite literally manually activate a regeneration cycle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: On older trucks, it is true that some trucks, unfortunately, you do have to pull over and you will have to manually hit a button.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: When you do that, what it does is it superheats the DPF and essentially burns off all of the chemicals that have been stored inside of this diesel particulate filter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: On most of these newer vehicles, however, and by newer, I mean pretty much anything after 2009, they also have the ability to do a passive regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: What that means is as the vehicle is simply driving around at highway speeds or on the West Side Highway or anything else, as they're driving around, it is literally burning off the excess chemicals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: in the DPF filter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I do want to note, when they actually go through the activity of doing an active regeneration, that regeneration is almost 30 times dirtier than a passive regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: At no point should anybody be doing an active regeneration in a heavily populated area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: It's incredibly dirty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: It's very dangerous for the health and humans in general, and it should not be done near populated areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: It's actually so dangerous that if you read the DPF filters for modern trucks, they specifically warn you, A, not to do it in your populated areas, and they also warn you not to do it near anything combustible or flammable, specifically because of the high heats and the chemicals emitted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I do also just want to note that there is a– this would create almost a situation where there would be an unrebuttable presumption.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: All an industry respondent would have to claim is we're regenerating.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: And guess what?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: How do we go about disproving it?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Most people–

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Even with my experience, I can maybe get it to 70%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: The average hearing officer or citizen complaint or anybody else who has had no experience with diesel trucks beyond, you know, filming or seeing them on the road, how are they ever going to determine that a vehicle is regenerated?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So you're saying it would just destroy the whole law itself if we could create an exemption for regeneration because...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: All any defense would be is we're regenerating, and it would be impossible to disprove their regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So that would result in more idling because...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: People just always use that defense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: And I would also note that this benefits the biggest respondents the most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: And what I mean by that is large truck and large bus companies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: So a smaller operation almost always, like most of my clients, small businesses, usually if you have less than 10 trucks, it is very common to have gasoline engines, simply because they're cheaper up front, cheaper to maintain over the long term, and the fuel is honestly cheaper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Gasoline vehicles would not be able to endure themselves with this particular exemption, but guess who would?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Large companies like Baldor, Academy Bus, and things like that that operate thousands of diesel engines.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it sounds like I understand this.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And thank you, Chair, for letting me ask a couple of questions here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, you've got a little more.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I think I'm good.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'll give you 15 seconds back.

chapters.summary: Gennaro thanks the panel for its testimony and says the hearing will continue with more witnesses. He calls the next panel including Zach Miller of the Trucking Association of New York, Larry Zogby of RDS Delivery, and Pat Hyland.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks panel and calls truck and bus panel

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm not going to give you a hard time, Harvey.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just, you know, do what you got to do.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, good.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I really want to thank this panel for their very excellent testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And Ryan, didn't you meet with us?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: Numerous times.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, no, no, but it was in the conference room with Hayden?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, oh, that was you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, that was a good information exchange session.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, we certainly did appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: And if I could say just, Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: You did ask us in the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ryan Scott-Loki
utterances.text: I do not believe 561A can be saved as currently written.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, that's your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is why I wanted to have the hearing to get testimony and to get what people really think about this.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so with that, we have a long day.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We have to get on to other panels.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We appreciate everyone being here.

chapters.summary: Gennaro calls the next panel and says he will take a short break while the panel assembles. He insists it is not a formal recess and that he wants to hear every word of testimony.
chapters.title: Gennaro calls truck and bus panel and takes short recess

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And now we have the next panel, which I'm going to call.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then I'm going to have to take just like a two-minute recess while the panel gets itself together.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Crowley, a former council member, represents union contractors through the Building Trades Employers Association. She says engines often power lifts, lighting, cranes, pumps, and decontamination showers, and asks the Council to support 561-A while holding 11-A.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Crowley of BTEA supports 561-A, 562, and 869-A but opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro, the members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: I know Council Member Harvey Epstein was here and the other.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, he's talking to witnesses outside.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: He's further interrogating them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And all the council members on the committee and the committee staff, thank you for the good work you do, your commitment of public service, the environment, and cleaner air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And thank you for allowing me to testify today and this opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: My name is Elizabeth Crowley, and I'm here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: I am the president and CEO of the Building Trades Employers Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: I have our director of member services here as well, Samuel Eludo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: The BTA is a union contractor association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We're an umbrella association that covers over 24 separate associations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And together, there's over 1,200 contractors that we represent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Many are small family-owned businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Many are also MW.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: and emerging contractors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We share the Council's commitment to cleaner air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We support the core reforms in Intro 561A as well as Intro 562 and proposed Intro 869A, but we cannot support Intro 11A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: as drafted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Our written testimony submitted today is more extensive and includes recommendations for each bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Our union contractors are proud to be paying higher wages and they are among the safest and most are community-minded employees, employers,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: and the best in their class, best in the industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And we're proud of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We're proud of the high standards our contractors set, not only for themselves, but their whole entire workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We live in your districts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Many of us are small businesses, as I said earlier, and we really care.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Liz, please continue.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You get the former council member bonus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: With the cost of doing business in the city.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: My council told me not to say that, but after I said it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: I appreciate this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Won't be too much longer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: But with the cost of doing business in the city so high, our contractors are very conscientious about wasting resources when their trucks are...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And it's often because the engine is needed to do a job, like running a lift gate, lighting the job site, powering a crane,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: a pump compressor, generator, the warning lights that protect a work zone, and even the decontamination showers that OSHA requires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: For those that are working on asbestos and lead abated jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: These functions cannot always be shut off between cycles without creating safety risks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: However, our contractors are often penalized for doing the work that is required of their job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Intro 561A's new processing device definition is a good step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: But it covers only equipment mechanically connected to the engine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We asked the council to define operational idling to include traffic control devices, generators, decontamination units, and the pauses safe operation requires,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: and to presume that when it is operating,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: It is visible work underway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Drivers waiting to enter a job site in extreme cold or heat also need a safe cab.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And to a 561A, let school buses idle for up to 30 minutes below 40 degrees and or at 80 or above.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We believe our workers deserve a comparable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: exception.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We know fundamentally the current enforcement process is really, we believe, unfair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: for our members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: The process encourages community vigilantes who put honest, hardworking union members in danger.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: The city bounty has turned enforcement into a business for a few high volume complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And we also, you know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: are here to continue to work for the committee.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I was hoping that your colleague could sort of pick up on your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Yeah, because I'm going to get in trouble.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: And I'm closing thanking you again, Chair Gennaro and Councilmember Epstein and the committee.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: We'll let you take over there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I'm going to have to give a, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just saying, some of the environmental people, I've got to give a little more time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's great to see you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's great to see you.

chapters.summary: Eluto says BTEA wants stronger definitions of operational idling and better evidence requirements. He says demolition, asbestos remediation, and other trades have equipment needs that current enforcement does not adequately recognize.
chapters.title: Samuel Eluto of BTEA seeks clearer operational-idling definitions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: But thank you, Council Member Epstein and Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: We're going to share recommendations.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, could you say your name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: Samuel Ludo, Director of Member Relations for the Building Trade Employers Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: I know Council Member Epstein acknowledged that the process is currently flawed to give notice to our contractors, and that's a priority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: But another priority is really understanding the oath mechanism to have that deliberation, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: There's been a discussion throughout this council hearing about what qualifies as idling, and we think that there should be stronger definitions, clarifications, enforcements, and also requirements for evidence because, you know, if our council...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: If we get notice, there's still discrepancies about what should be considered operational idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: And, you know, our members, 24 different associations, we have, you know, everything from decontamination units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: So, you know, when you're cleaning out asbestos, you need to have that kind of working, you know, engine running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: But even, you know, one of our members, the demolition contractors, in order to take all that garbage, you have to do things like compress it, which necessarily isn't captured in these other discussions about what is considered

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: operational idling, what is considered the regeneration process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: My understanding is it's a little bit different for demolition contractors or it's a little bit different for asbestos and remediation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: So, you know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: The bus guys have their own thing going on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: There's other things, but, you know, we're going to send very specific recommendations, which we think are, you know, we think there should be good, you know, environmental, you know, remediation and good environmental justice policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: But we also think that our members shouldn't be unfairly targeted by policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, yeah, I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: BTEA, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: BTEA, right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you both.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, oh, here we go.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Here we go.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Here we go.

chapters.summary: Miller says the complaint program has become a profitable cottage industry while businesses face stacked citations and delayed notice. He supports 561-A's recognition of refrigeration and loading equipment, supports 562 and 869-A, and opposes 11-A's penalty increase.
chapters.title: Zach Miller of Trucking Association supports 561-A and 562, opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro, Councilmember Epstein.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Don't break the thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I think I already did.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I'm Vice President of Affairs for the Trucking Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We submitted detailed written comments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I'll highlight our priorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Our industry does not condone unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Eileen Taney did not oppose the Citizens Air Complaint Program when it was first enacted, but it has gone off the rails, becoming a profitable

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: cottage industry for individuals while businesses face stacked citations, delayed notice, barriers to challenge evidence that undermines confidence in enforcement and the ability to change behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Taney strongly supports Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: It recognizes necessary equipment operation, including refrigerated units and loading and unloading devices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Exempts require diesel particulate filter regeneration, which a report can be generated by the vehicle's ECM to prove if it was in regen or if it was not in regen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And in addition to that, we support Intro 562.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Rental leasing companies should not bear responsibility for conduct they cannot control.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Transfer of liability must be simple, affordable, and operational before penalty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We support Intro 869A's protections against fraudulent evidence and complaint misconduct.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We oppose Intro 11A's penalty increase at this time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Advance the reforms first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Restore accountability and especially due process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Evaluate the results before increasing penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We look forward to working with the council and the DEP on improvements, and I look forward to your questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Zach.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Zogby, a pleasure to see you again.

chapters.summary: Zogby of RDS Delivery says idling hearings have been scheduled 500 to 962 days after violations. He asks for notices within 30 to 45 days, hearings within 90 days, no repeat penalties before notice, and defined 60-minute Zoom hearing windows.
chapters.title: Larry Zogby describes two-year hearing delays and proposes four fixes

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: My name is Larry Zogby, the CEO of RDS Delivery Service.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We handle time-critical medical deliveries for hospitals and laboratories, including specimens, medication, and essential supplies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We also deliver thousands of food boxes to New Yorkers facing food insecurity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: I've served five years as the president of the New York State Messenger Courier Association, also involved with the Trucking Association of New York, the Queens Chamber of Commerce, the Long Island City Partnership, Executives Association of New York, and Entrepreneurs Organization of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: I speak only for RDS, but these concerns go beyond myself, my business, my community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: 30 selected idling summonses from 2020 through 2025, over $32,000 in fines and penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Hearings were scheduled 500, 700, and 962 days after the violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: That's more than two and a half years later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Idling fines start at $350, go to $600 for repeat offense, and can reach upwards to $2,000.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: My question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: How can a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: business correct violations promptly when hearings take years and penalties grow so dramatically.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We're asking for four practical changes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Mail notices within 30 to 45 days showing the mailing date.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Schedule hearings within 90 days with advance reminders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Don't increase fines for repeat violations until a business has been notified

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: for the first one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Provide a defined 60-minute Zoom hearing window.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We're not asking to eliminate enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We're asking for a fair opportunity to comply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: When a hearing takes 962 days and penalties can grow from $350 to $2,000, something's wrong within the process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Enforcement should correct behavior, not simply accumulate penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: RDS strongly opposes Intro 11 and supports Intros 561, 562, and proposed Intro 869.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Thank you for your consideration.

chapters.summary: Gennaro asks Zogby to explain how delayed notices create multiple violations before a business knows about the first one. Zogby says drivers may be gone by the time notices arrive, making corrective action impossible.
chapters.title: Gennaro questions Zogby on stacked violations and inability to correct drivers

utterances.text: Yeah, we are seeing some behaviors change or whatever, but...

utterances.text: You know, we can't be having this years-long process.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: During this, so when you, so what happens is, you know,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: you would be notified of a bunch of violations like at one time saying that this, so you got a first violation, second violation, third violation, and this is, and you never knew you even got the first one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the second violation, third violation, you know, accrue penalties and you have to.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Deal with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We can't even reconstruct the penalty, and the driver's not even there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Driver could be gone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: There's turnover.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Driver could stay for a year, year and a half.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We're not getting these violations for over one year, two years, 500, 700, EBIT, 962 days after the violation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And now certainly you train your staff, you know, to do whatever you want them to do, like regarding idling.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: In terms of calling a driver to task because they were idling or whatever, by the time you get the violation, it could be that there's turnover, the person's not there anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So in terms of trying to correct staff behavior, this...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is another reason why this lapse in processing is a big deal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: It's the due process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: If we make a mistake, we're more than happy to right the game.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We want to comply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: But how do you comply when it's two and a half years later?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, I think Zach wants to get in on it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I will formally ask Zach if you can expand.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, Harvey's going to get you too.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Is evidence, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Like we talked about in the last panel about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: There are defenses.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sergeant, can we get a better microphone?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It looks like we've got a microphone that's on the fritz.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Companies don't maintain those records for two years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: So by the time a company will get the summons, they could have been.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Having a legitimate reason to idle, but they no longer have the evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: That's why we need to get the due process right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And we also need access to the videos right away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: If you look at the red light camera program, that's a program that works incredibly well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Respondent is notified properly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: They are able to access the video and they're able to determine if it is worth contesting or if they are guilty and pay the penalty and change their behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We do not have that opportunity in this program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And that's what Larry was talking about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: That is what all of Tanny's membership has been saying for years and years and years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: It is a due process problem.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm good from my end.

chapters.summary: Epstein asks whether OATH is the source of delay and whether businesses can get video evidence sooner. Miller and Zogby say OATH is hard to reach, notices can default without receipt, and access to video would let companies decide whether to contest.
chapters.title: Epstein questions panel on OATH delays and repeat-offense defaults

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I recognize Councilmember Epstein for questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Thanks for, like, hanging out and being here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: No, sure.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Happy to.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This is an interesting issue that we all got to solve together.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it sounds like everyone agrees that oath is a problem, right?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Is that what we hear everyone saying?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Oath isn't notifying you quickly enough.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Oath is not prosecuting these cases quickly enough.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So you don't even...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Know to maintain information if you don't even know until six months later that there was a problem.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Is that what everyone's saying?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Samuel Eluto
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So one, it sounds like figuring out a way to get notification to go out quickly.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Two is to get access to that video evidence quickly and to make a decision whether you just want to plead guilty and move on or not plead guilty because you think it's not a true violation.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: What does Oath say when you flag these issues for them?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: They don't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: We can't get a hold.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: There's no numbers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: There's no answer.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: There's a commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: She's the former DCWP commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: She now runs Oath.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: She's, you know, a person who meets with people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Can I make a– and you are a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Can you– would you be willing to spend some time with one of our members as they adjudicate a hearing to Oath so you see exactly what that process, or I should say lack thereof, looks like?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm happy to.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And I've actually appeared in front of Oath on behalf– you know, I've–

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I was a legal services lawyer, so I had a very different job, but I would appear in front of Oath when I was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: and tenants were trying to get landlords to do things, and Oath wasn't prosecuting those cases.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But I'm happy to follow up with one of your members to hear what's happening at Oath.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I think there's a lot of issues that we're grappling with that could be fixed at Oath's level that I think would help this problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Crowley
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: And the other one, and I'm sorry to jump in, Zach, is that they're doubling, tripling, quadrupling the fines before we even know.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So when it's written, if there's no existing violation, it's written as a first violation unless there's an adjudication and a fine.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So it's only if it's being written again that they could have four or five that are pending, but you already have to have a violation to be considered as a repeat offender, right?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So if they're writing five violations and there's no history of violations, they're all written as first violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: You have a fleet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: You have one car.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: They're in Wall Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: They get a violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We never get it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Same car as in Wall Street gets a second, gets a third violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We don't know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We can't take action.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You're saying because once a fleet gets a violation, that's a repeat offender, you're saying?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Or the car gets a violation, it's a repeat offender?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: The same car gets a repeat offense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: We never know about it.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: But if there's a violation that you've been adjudicated already, that's only when you get repeat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Liz, can we just get that microphone down here for a second?

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This information is not getting on the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Right, but sometimes what happens is you never receive the summons at all, but it's in the oath system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: So you are found guilty by non-appearance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And all of a sudden you're a repeat offender, even though you have never received the summons.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: So there's two issues.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: One is violations happening.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Two is not knowing what's happening.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And three is not getting these systems processed quickly enough.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I think there's some shared...

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Ground there that we could all collectively, if the chair is open to it, to work on.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Because I think we want these, we want you to know, we want you to educate the drivers, we want this to move quickly, and we want to make sure that these don't happen and that businesses who are trying to do the right thing

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: Don't get repeat fines if this is not an appropriate idling violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: Yeah, I really do appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: And the last point I do want to make is about 562A because it is a huge problem for the rental and leasing companies as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: For them to have to go back years, try to track down who was operating that vehicle at the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: You know, the companies who they partner with are the ones who keep the records.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: It doesn't go, but the rental and leasing companies who don't operate the equipment don't have those records.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: The transfer viability, as it does exist in most other enforcement programs in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Miller
utterances.text: city is another important part of the due process.

chapters.summary: Gennaro thanks the panel and says their testimony added important detail about due-process failures. He then moves to the next panel.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks truck and bus panel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I want to...

utterances.text: I would just...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Rubbing you a little, Larry, because this is not kind of like a grab the mic kind of like forum here, you know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: I'm the first time here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Larry Zogby
utterances.text: No, second.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Anyway, really appreciate, you know, your insight and what's going on.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, everybody on this panel, great to see you, Liz.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we appreciate the value added from this panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: The next panel is going to look at it a little differently, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You bet.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You did a great job.
