chapters.summary: Brockett says he joins more than 30 environmental and good-government groups opposing 561-A. He argues the bill's 60-day deadline and reduced awards would undermine the program while Intro 48 would expand access.
chapters.title: Hayden Brockett opposes 561-A and warns it would gut the complaint program

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: All right, great.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's north, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's north.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I forget which.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I get turned around down here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's north.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: My name is Hayden Brockett, and I join with over 30 environmental and good government groups, as well as two committees on Manhattan Community Board 7, which I serve, to oppose Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: The Citizens Air Complaint Program, make no mistake, is working well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: It is stopping pollution all across our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: There is coverage that tracks pollution, and we cannot go backwards on clean air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: But unfortunately, that is exactly what this council is poised to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I want to talk about what would happen if the suite of bills up for today passes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just going to jump in for a second.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'll give you time at the end.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But it's just, you know, these are not being presented as like final.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We want to pass some bills.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: These are all works in progress.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So it's like these are all.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're hearing them because they're not done.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We, you know, they're not where we want them to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I hear you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: There have been some edits and amendments that have been made that unfortunately make the make it worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And I don't think that's a secret that there are problems.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I think that I think that's fine testimony, but it's just like we're not, you know, like we're not angling to pass these bills tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: OK, that's good to know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: If Intro 48 were passed to open up the Citizens Air Complaint Program to the 2.5 million New Yorkers who don't speak English, that would be good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: They've been locked out of the program since the Adams administration, and it sounds good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: But unfortunately, Intro 561A slams that same door shut with dangerous new loopholes that effectively legalize all diesel engine idling, all school bus idling for half the year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And it requires the DEP throw out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Now it sounds like 230,000 pending complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And going forward, throw out many other complaints because they can't meet that deadline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: You may as well not have a program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And it's terrible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: For our air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And to add insult to that very real and life-threatening injury, those 2.5 million New Yorkers who got their first

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: shot at participation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: This council would say, sorry.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, just keep going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: You don't get the same portion of the fines that has been on the books for the last 55 years because Intro 561A is now cutting citizen awards just as you get to participate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And I think that sends a terrible message to those New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: The bill cannot be resurrected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I do want to talk about Intro 11A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: I think it sounds good that it raises fines for corporate polluters, but unfortunately it's going to undermine compliance because all but the biggest violators will skip out on those fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: Today, the stats show nearly 40% of idling violators ignore their tickets, which, let's be clear, run from $350 to $600.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: They just don't pay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And collection attempts are unfortunately not successful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: So there's a $3,000 fine in Intro 11A, and that message, unfortunately, does not send compliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: It's too high.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: The message is that it's all for show.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett
utterances.text: And I think, in fact, you're going to have less compliance if the fines are too high.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hayden Brockett

chapters.summary: Caballero says translating the portal would help her mother and other limited-English-proficiency New Yorkers report pollution. She argues 561-A's 60-day rule and regeneration exemption would create backdoor ways to dismantle enforcement.
chapters.title: Alicia de Carmen Caballero supports 48 and rejects 561-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Hi there, my name is Alicia de Carmen Caballero and I participate in the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: I support Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Translating the portal would help people like my mom, whose first language is not English, and would expand protection of our air quality to communities that are not being sufficiently covered and protected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Your ability to protect your community should never depend on the language that you speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: However, it is shameful that just as we are opening up this program to immigrant communities, Intro 561A would effectively shut it down through the back door.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: It would do that in two ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: The first is the 60-day requirement would force DEP to throw out violations that it can't process in 60 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: It's currently taking around 12 months to process those violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: This means that a year's worth of pollution violations would be tossed in the bin, and in effect, no new violations would ever be able to be processed in the future because DEP just currently isn't staffed to meet that kind of timeline.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Polluters would get a free pass, and we would lose our ability to protect our air quality going forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Pollution doesn't become less harmful just because...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: because the violation sat in somebody's inbox for too long.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Second thing is diesel regeneration exemption would allow idling when a truck is burning off soot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: But there is no way for me or the DEP reviewer to confirm whether that truck was actually doing that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: So the result is that any time an idling truck gets a violation, they can just say, I was doing diesel regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: There'd be no way to disprove it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: So it's a get-out-of-jail-free card.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: So again, polluters would get a pass, and we would lose this important mechanism to enforce our clean air laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: So these are backdoor ways of dismantling enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: One lets the clock excuse pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: The other creates a loophole that residents cannot challenge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Both of my parents were truck drivers, long-haul truck drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: They also deserve clean air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Everybody in this room does, whether you're an environmentalist or from the industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: So my ask is to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Please pass Intro 48 and reject Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Wholly, I don't think it's resurrectable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: I think the one thing that needs to change is better staffing for the DEP to get through these violations more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: And please don't invite immigrant communities into this program, only to strip it of its power to protect them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alicia de Carmen Caballero
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Zaidi says citizen idling enforcement brought camera-like deterrence to air pollution. He suggests DEP can already send warning letters with video links and prioritize leasing companies in the backlog without legislation.
chapters.title: Rafil Zaidi compares idling enforcement to red-light cameras and suggests DEP stopgaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Red light and speed cameras were kind of a watershed moment for traffic enforcement in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: No longer could vehicle operators, unless they got particularly unlucky, count on breaking the law without consequence, which is still the case for most moving violations and administrative infractions of all kinds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Idling enforcement, which uses the eyes, ears, and phones of citizens throughout the city instead of stationary cameras, brought a roughly comparable level of enforcement to vehicular air pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: As with the robot cameras, not for every block, intersection, or hour of the day, but enough to make operators think twice and not break the law in the first place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: The response?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Greater city revenue, greater compliance, and also some pushback.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Sound familiar?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: The New York Post reported back in 2024 that the resulting vehicle plate defacement by scofflaws was soaring and costing the city $200 million a year in uncollected tolls and tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Did council start seriously entertaining a bill to legalize ghost plates or restrict the use of ticketing cameras?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: But private car drivers worried about tickets, myself included, don't have the lobbyists that the trucking and bus industries do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: So now those industries are complaining that they don't like the fines they're getting for breaking the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: and that they'd like to go back to the good old days when getting an idling ticket was the equivalent of getting struck by lightning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: The question should not be why is there so much enforcement in these particular areas, but why isn't there better enforcement in other areas where public health and safety

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: I'd like to address summons delays and transfer of liability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: DEP has the ability already for a stopgap, as long as they have a backlog, to batch equipment leasing companies for priority reviews so that those fines can be passed along, and also to send non-summons heads-up letters to the named respondents as soon as new citizen complaints come in,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: along with access to the video evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: I agree with Zach Miller 100% on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: It's basically about flipping a switch in a computer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Let's tell DEP to do it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: 561, 562, and 869 would be destructive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: 11A would act as cover.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: In this context, in combination with 561A, that would be like saying we're going to double the speed camera fines, oh, and also we're going to remove 95% of speed cameras.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: DEP already has the authority to increase fines reasonably.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Only Intro 48 would improve the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: I volunteered training air complaint program participants in the South Bronx, so I've seen that firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro asks Zaidi to repeat what DEP could do without a law change. Zaidi says DEP could adjust fines, send heads-up letters with video access, and prioritize certain complaints for review.
chapters.title: Gennaro asks Zaidi to explain DEP actions that could start immediately

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your good testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You were talking about how DEP now has the ability to do what tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I was trying to follow along.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Could you just go over that again?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: There are a couple of things, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Is that they can adjust the fine schedule without a legislative change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Another is that there are a variety of solutions that can be pursued as stopgaps to ensure reasonable notification times for respondents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: That would include sending a heads-up letter to the named respondent in a complaint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Along with access to the video, as soon as that comes in, that can be auto-generated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Maybe they could save on the bulk first-class mailing by doing it only to fleets that haven't received penalties before, but why not do everyone?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: It's a drop in the bucket compared to the overall income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Finally, I was trying to keep the interests of equipment leasing companies in mind.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: Where DEP already batches certain hearings for priority, certain complaints for priority review, batches priority hearings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: For example, for Con Ed, you know, that might happen in a month or two as opposed to 900 days for other people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that they know who a lot of the equipment leasing companies are, that they have a particular interest in passing along fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: There's nothing stopping them from having a filter in place to prioritize those for review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rafil Zaidi
utterances.text: As another way to address some of the problems from the ongoing backlog.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, I certainly appreciate that excellent testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And this is why we're having this hearing, and thank you for your valued addition to it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Kevin McGee, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, sure.

chapters.summary: McGee says he participates in the program in his spare time and has seen major fleets like Con Edison, Amazon, and Verizon reduce idling. He urges the Council to reject 561-A and support Intro 48.
chapters.title: Kevin McGee says the complaint program changes fleet behavior

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: I'm a participant in this program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: I have a day job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: I do this in some spare time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Last time I testified about 941, you were fascinated about my interest in doing this because I walk 12 miles a day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: It's something that I was already doing before.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: How many miles a day?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: 12 miles a day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: I was already doing it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: You were fascinated before when I testified about 941.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Councilmember Villas already cited the figure 2,400 deaths a year from air pollution in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Illegal wildlife contributes to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: It's very much preventable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: And I believe, as a participant in this program, that the citizen complaint program works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: This law was practically unenforced for almost four decades, has finally some teeth to it with this program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Could you speak a little louder or closer to the mic?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: As participants, we've watched major fleets change their behavior, including Con Ed, Amazon, Verizon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: We do not see them idling nearly as much as we used to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Because this enforcement changes behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: But air pollution has a particularly cruel future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Its consequences are indirect, and its victims are easy to overlook.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: A child in an under-resourced neighborhood has an asthma attack.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Someone develops lung cancer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Older New Yorker dies of stroke or heart disease earlier than they would have otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: And we rarely see that connection because

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it just makes it easier for elected officials to fail to protect them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: and to ignore it without consequence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: But these are not abstract statistics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: These are real people and real lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: And I apologize for the sort of grim analogy here, but if a gunman walked into a school and exacted a quota every year wiping out a classroom, we would not accept that as a minor policy tradeoff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: We would not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Accept that as a bargaining chip in regular political horse trading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: So the victims of pollution deserve no less urgency, simply because their suffering is less visible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: So I would urge you to reject 561A in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: I do not think it's redeemable, but support Intro 48 to bring this program to the communities that need it the most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: And to use Councilmember Velasquez's analogy, this would not put the program 10 toes down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: It would put it six feet under.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin McGee
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Welde compares annual air-pollution deaths to traffic and gun fatalities and says idling is the largest single source of illegal air pollution. He argues 561-A would violate the state constitution's right to clean air and urges a no vote.
chapters.title: Ernest Welde opposes 11, 561, 562, and 869 and supports 48

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: My name is Ernest Weldy, and I'm speaking in opposition to intros 11, 561, 562, and 869, and in favor of 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: I'll focus on 561.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: It is unrecoverable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Over the past five years, there have been about 250 traffic-related fatalities per year for a total of 1,264.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: There have been about 400 homicides by gun per year for a total of 1,990.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Over that same time period, according to the Department of Health and today's testimony, there have been approximately 2,400 deaths due to poor air quality every year for a total of 12,000 people, plus countless other health issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: The Department of Health attributes these two to just two air pollutants, ozone and PM2.5.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: The largest contributor in New York City of these pollutants is idling vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: In fact, idling is the largest single source of illegal air pollution in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Just to put this in context, if there were 2,400 murders by gun in New York City every year, the governor would likely call the Nats.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: National Guard, and it would be the singular focus of city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: But what does city council do when confronted with 2,400 deaths per year?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: They call a hearing to minimize the best program that is actually reducing that staggering death toll.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: You have heard over and over today how effective this program is in reducing illegal idling in New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: In fact, it's really the only street-level environmental law that is enforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: There have been virtually zero tickets for plastic bags, straw and demands, open doors during AC season.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: You guys are great at passing laws, but the city is awful at enforcing them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Intro 561 violates the state constitution, Article 1, Section 19.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: It's short but straightforward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Each person shall have a right to clean air and water and a healthful environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: This bill, if passed, would clearly violate this provision of the state constitution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: There has been no analysis as to what this will do to the air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: 30 minutes of idling in front of a school for small children who are among the most affected by poor air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Unlimited diesel idling for regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: If this bill is passed, it will definitely decrease the quality of New York City's air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: You must not violate your duty to protect our environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: It's incredible with all the environmental issues facing the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: We're focused on rolling back protections for New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: This is a polluter-friendly bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: It would give billion-dollar corporations a major break.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: It would be sad to take away if the takeaway here was that city council is protecting polluters by harming New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: This doesn't make the program better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: We need to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: change the program in some ways, but not this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Don't disincentivize reporters by lowering the citizen share.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: Please vote no on 11, 561, 562, 869, and yes on 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ernest Welde
utterances.text: And I'm curious if you could talk about why you think the program isn't working, as you said earlier.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, we ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hang on.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Nicholas?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Day says Edge has received more than 175 idling summonses this year and absorbed about $60,000 in penalties for customer conduct. He supports Intro 562, supports procedural protections in 561-A, and opposes 11-A until the system is fixed.
chapters.title: Nicholas Day of Edge Auto Rental seeks liability transfer under 562

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Thank you, and thanks for giving us the time to be here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: My name is Nicholas Day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: I'm the co-CEO of Edge Auto Rental.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We're an independent, employee-owned vehicle rental company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We employ approximately 60 people here in New York, and we've been in business here for 40 years.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't know what we do now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's just...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: So those things don't plug into anything, the mics?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Testing, testing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: This year alone, Edge has received more than 175 idling summonses totaling over $80,000.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We've recovered about $20,000 from our customers, leaving our company to absorb approximately $60,000 of penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: The problem is we didn't idle the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Our customers did.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We weren't driving them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: They're not our employees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We're not operating the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We had no ability to prevent these violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We're the ones being penalized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Making matters worse, as we've heard earlier today, summonses routinely arrive six months to more than a year after the alleged violation, long after the rental has ended and our customer has disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Many of our trucks must run their engines, as we've heard earlier today, to operate equipment, including lift gates and refrigerating systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: That's not unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: That's doing the work the vehicles were designed to perform.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We're asking the council to take three important steps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: First, pass Introduction 562, allowing liability to transfer from rental companies to the actual renters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Second, adopt the procedural protections in 561A, including timely notices and recognition of legitimate engine-required operations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: And third, do not increase the penalties under 11A until these fundamental problems are corrected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Edge hasn't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: invested millions of dollars in clean vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We want to be part of the solution, but environmental enforcement should punish the party responsible for the violation, not the business that happens to own the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: We respectfully ask the council to fix the system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nicholas Day
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You painted a portrait of a system that is not

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: working the way it should and so that's why we're here today and we value your your your you know on the ground understanding of what this all means to businesses you bet

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Glenn every

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Bus Association of New York State?

chapters.summary: Avery says private motor coaches are subject to citizen enforcement while public transit buses are not. He argues modern coaches need engines for safety and passenger comfort and opposes Intro 11-A's higher fines.
chapters.title: Glenn Avery of BANI opposes bus inclusion in idling enforcement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm Glenn Avery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: I'm president of the Bus Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: We're also known as BANI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: And we've been around as an organization since 1938.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: And we're proud to advocate on behalf of private bus operators and the public.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: The riding public that they serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Banning is opposed to the inclusion of motor coaches under the anti-idling restrictions under the Citizens Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Unlike the buses operated by our members, public transit buses are not subject to enforcement under the Citizens Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: They use the same equipment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: They have the same compliance difficulties that our members have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: So the net result is that private operators who have far fewer buses on New York City streets than public transit are the only target of enforcement against buses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: This is revenue generation, not sound environmental policy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Modern motor coaches are designed with a main diesel engine that only provides for the propulsion of the vehicle, but also power safety,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: the HVA system, environmental, electrical, and other systems that are necessary for the safe operation of the vehicle, the health and well-being of passengers, and the protection of the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Until technology develops to the point where that fundamental design can be changed, compliance with the three-minute rule can be very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: We are not advocates for unlimited or unnecessary idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: To the contrary, our members, they don't want to waste fuel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: They don't condone that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: I would like to just kind of jump off my script if I could.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Yeah, sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: To address a specific request that you made that we talk about specifics about 11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: We are opposed to intro 11A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: The increasing of fines is of little additional deterrence value.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: The fines are already at a level where motor coach operators are choosing to avoid New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I just said two other points.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Why don't we just finish the panel, and I'm formulating a question for you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Patrick, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Patrick.

chapters.summary: Condren says buses are the most environmentally efficient passenger vehicles and should be exempt from idling fines like public buses. He calls the three-minute rule untenable and cites a 15-minute federal guideline for buses.
chapters.title: Patrick Condren asks that private buses be treated like public buses

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Patrick, just state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: I am Patrick Condren.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: I'm the administrator of the Bus for NYC Coalition, which was formed in 2018 to address issues in my industry, which I'm lifelong in the bus industry and a member of BANI and a board member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: At that time in 2018, congestion pricing was an issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: And unfortunately,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Many people do not be exempt in the area, but all buses, intercity, commuter, and our operators are exempt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: We're part of the public and private position and transportation, providing public transportation in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: I was one of the owners of the franchise bus companies back in the day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: I work with the guys today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: So having said that, a bus is the most environmentally efficient passenger vehicle on the streets of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Regarding oversight of the Citizens Air Complaint Group, we support changes in this program, as Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Evry just pointed out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: And it's a reminder that bus lines...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Rail lines, airlines, or passenger carryings, not cargo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: The issue today is New York City policy includes buses as part of the public system, just like the MTA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: because all the MTA buses were routes in all of Queens and Brooklyn where I was.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: And there's 170 miles of bus lanes because all public ride the bus lanes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: And they're not exempt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: It's just we use them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Trucks don't use them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Cars don't use them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Everybody at this panel earlier today referred to cars and trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: It's our position that just like congestion pricing, just like parking, ICBPS, and numerous other city rules, that private buses, just like public buses, should be administratively exempt from the actual fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: Today, there's millions of dollars and thousands of tickets being issued to private bus companies, as Glenn pointed out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: don't even want to come into New York City anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: So the three-minute rule is untenable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: The federal guideline is 15 minutes for a bus to idle if they had to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Condren
utterances.text: And we believe that at this point in time, people should be reminded that 55 people on a bus is the most environmentally sound vehicle on the streets of New York, and they're included with and they should be treated the same as publicly owned buses.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro asks Avery to finish his point about 561-A. Avery says the bill exempts temperature-sensitive cargo and asks that human passengers be treated as temperature-sensitive too, especially in extreme heat or cold.
chapters.title: Gennaro asks Avery about temperature-sensitive cargo and passenger comfort

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Before I pose questions to this panel, if I call Josh up for a second, I have to just come up to the dais.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just have to talk to you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just come up to the front here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It was just I need a candy bar.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's a sugar thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So and.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Avery, right, I want to ask you about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You were just on the cusp of telling me something that you think I should know, and I want to ask you what that is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Yeah, just addressing the specifics of 561, if I'm correct, I believe it expands the definition of processing device.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: And it also exempts systems that, quote, control the environment of temperature-sensitive cargo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: I would ask that you consider that human beings be considered temperature-sensitive cargo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: To put human beings in a bus that's over 100 degrees because it's been sitting in the hot sun where the windows can't come down and we can't, you know, the driver can't turn the air conditioning on for an appropriate amount of time, that's...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, because, like, we're doing that for school buses and stuff.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Glenn Avery
utterances.text: Same thing on the cold side.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, let me just hang out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Let me just talk to counsel for a second.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I just want to clarify a point with her, you know, regarding.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Regarding Patrick's testimony, but she made that clear to me.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I want to thank this panel for all the value added that you've provided to it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, the whole bus thing, you know, how we handle that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we look forward to being in touch with everybody on this panel on how we can proceed along lines of excellence.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sounds like something a politician would say, but that's actually what I mean.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you all very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're happy to follow up.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.
