chapters.summary: David, a Hell's Kitchen resident with asthma, says 561-A would weaken a successful air-quality program. He says he understands both sides and hopes everyone ends the day healthy.
chapters.title: Timothy David opposes 561-A and calls for health-focused compromise

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: Chair members, my name is Timothy David, and I am a resident of Hell's Kitchen and have long time asthma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: I am here today to speak in opposition to proposed 5561A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: because it would weaken one of the New York City's most successful air quality enforcement programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: I have crossed some things out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: From hearing everyone, I really do appreciate everyone's testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: and as well as their input.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: And I duly understand both sides.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: And I'm speaking for myself on behalf of my spouse, who is a member of the New York Clean Air Collective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: And for every day, for many hours, listening and observing all the things that they go through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: I do wish at the end of the day, everyone

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: will be as healthy and well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: And that's all what I think we all wish for every individual.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Timothy David
utterances.text: And thank you very much again for your time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, for kind of...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: For, you know, this is, you know, I think your testimony was kind of like a mission statement for, I think, everybody in this room.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're coming from different perspectives, but we, you know, want to have as safe and environmentally friendly and pollution-free.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, New York City as we possibly can, given the fact that the 8.5 million people that live here and the God knows how many people who are here during every weekday that come into Manhattan to work,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: it's a challenge to...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, get everything right, but it's always nice to come back and touch home plate.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I think that's what you did for us here today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You bet.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Best to your wife.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Eileen.

chapters.summary: Spinner says she has asthma and that anti-idling laws went largely unenforced for decades until citizens stepped up. She opposes 561-A as a corporate giveaway, supports Intro 48, and says the mayor could expand language access without legislation.
chapters.title: Eileen Spinner supports the complaint program and opposes 561-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: My name is Eileen Spinner, and I'm here to support the Citizens Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, if you could speak a little closer to the mic, that'd be great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: I'm here to support the Citizens Air Complaint Program, which is working very, very well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: I have asthma, and the nearly 50 years that nobody bothered to enforce the anti-idling laws on the books probably didn't help with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: The city's anti-idling laws have only really been enforced in the past seven years, and only because citizens have stepped up to do this important work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: I am testifying against the very dangerous Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: At least 25 different environmental and civic groups oppose this bill because it's nothing less than a corporate giveaway by the city council to polluters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: It also opens up a dangerous loophole for diesel regeneration, which is an extremely dirty process, especially in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: There's a reason it's already illegal to regenerate while idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: Keep it that way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: To be clear, we must expand access to this program to all New Yorkers, including the 2.5 million who don't speak English as a first language.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: In fact, while I strongly support Intro 48, it isn't really necessary because the mayor could fix his predecessor's misguided policy today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: I also support raising fines, but again, Intro 11 doesn't need to exist at all because the mayor's administration has the power under the law to raise fines already.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: We cannot go backwards on clean air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: In fact, I am very troubled that this hearing is even happening today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: Who is supporting?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: This bill has zero co-sponsors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: The council staff amended this bill in response to criticism, and the amendments made it worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: As drafted, Intro 561 will effectively legalize diesel engine idling and give $100 million to polluting corporations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: If there's a battle of wills between the council and the mayor, I say stop playing politics with our health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: I implore you not to pass 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eileen Spinner
utterances.text: Let's not turn the clock back on clean air and good health.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your compelling testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hi, just a hold.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just I have to talk to counsel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you only knew what we were just talking about.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Should I put this on the record?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Just so you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, and so it was, yeah, please just talk right into the mic and proceed with, state your name for the record and proceed with your testimony.

chapters.summary: Pakenham says he produced the documentary 'Idle Threat' and has fought idling for 20 years. He argues 561-A favors trucking and bus profits over public health and urges the Council to reject it.
chapters.title: George Pakenham opposes 561-A and cites his anti-idling documentary

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: My name is George Packenham, and I'm a filmmaker and a producer of the documentary film Idle Threat, Man on a Mission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: And I'm a board member of the governor emeritus of the New York Clean Air Collective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: I'm 76 years old, and 20 years ago, I became aware of the pesky problem of air pollution caused by needless engine idling and have been fighting the fight ever since.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: The trucking and bus companies have their arguments in support of Bill 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: But I think they are after higher profits and less government oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: I oppose Bill 561A because it threatens to destroy all the good work that the New York Clean Air Collective has done fighting air pollution in this fair city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: I contend that the Clean Air, that the Citizens Air Complaint Program fights for a better public health and that that is the core argument here, not profits or government oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: I suggest that any council members who are curious about the facts and figures behind engine idling as a public health issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: Please visit the Environmental Defense Fund website and look at the study called Idling Gets You Nowhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: It's a comprehensive research document.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: And if you need a more practical approach to this problem, I have a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: When the meeting concludes, go outside on Broadway, find an idling bus, take a deep breath,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: And afterwards, it should be clear to you that Bill 561A should not pass city council vote in its current state and become law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - George Pakenham
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate you being here and being patient and giving us the benefit of your views.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And hang on.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Dietmar?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Dietmar?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I just have a confession to make.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm having like a sugar episode, and so I have to eat a candy bar as I'm listening to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But, yeah, I'm so, I apologize, but it's, if I'm going to be, you know, continue sitting upright, I have to.

chapters.summary: Detering says he is an active Queens complaint reporter and has seen fleets change behavior. He supports Intro 48's language access but says 561-A, 562, and 869-A would weaken enforcement and that 11-A's penalties are too aggressive.
chapters.title: Dietmar Detering supports 48 but opposes 561-A, 562, 869-A, and 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Your health first.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Your health first.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Cheers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Thank you for the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: My name is Dietmar Detering.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: I'm a Queens resident and an active citizen air complaint reporter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: The City Council should be proud of what the citizen air complaint program has accomplished.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: For decades, commercial trucks and buses routinely idled on our streets with little enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Today,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Many fleets have changed their behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: New Yorkers can already see, hear, and breathe the difference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Enforcement is increasingly reaching the fleets that have not yet adapted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Instead of complying, however, some are seeking relief from the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Interest 561A, 562,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: and 869A would provide that relief for polluters and move us in the wrong direction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: They would weaken enforcement and discourage citizen participation just when the program is beginning to realize its potential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Entry 11A is not the solution either.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Aggressive penalties raise the stakes for drivers and complainants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: encouraging confrontation and non-payment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: A reasonable inflation adjustment would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: I support Intro 48's expansion of language access, but accessibility also requires timely feedback and training.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Thousands of New Yorkers have registered for this program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: How many gave up?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Because DEP took over a year to tell them their complaints were defective.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: We need more successful citizen reporters, not fewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Broader participation will encourage greater compliance, leaving fewer violations for anyone to report.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Above all, DEP needs the resources

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: and direction to process complaints within the existing 45-day period.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Respondents should learn about violations promptly while they can change their behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: The Council should let this successful program mature rather than undermine it halfway through transforming New York City's idling culture.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dietmar Detering
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says he has learned a lot about what DEP could do to reduce its backlog and thanks witnesses for attending. He says the Council must improve the program and calls the next panel.
chapters.title: Gennaro reflects on what he has learned and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, we're, well, I'm certainly, you know, learning a lot at this hearing about what DEP could and should do to get rid of its backlog.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I'm just very happy that so many people came out to give us the benefit of their views.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, I might eat a candy bar during a hearing, but I'm not all.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I listen to every word and I'm very grateful to the staff, both in the audience and on the dais here, who are processing every word that is spoken.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I never passed a bad environmental law and after 18 years of chairing this committee, we've had a lot of hard challenges.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is a very hard one.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Everybody can do more, and we just have to figure out whether, because it's just, we're all jammed up.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: People get noticed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It just, anyway, I'm carrying on, but it's just, the purpose of what I'm saying is that I, you know, I'm attesting.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That we will work with all of you to try to get the best result we possibly can.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What we have right now is not working the way it could.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so we need to do better.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I think everybody agrees on that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so let's go out there and do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And this council and this panel helped us down that road.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I did not buy candy bars for everyone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Is that Pablo?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hey, man.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I didn't forget you, Cadillac.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's a person, but his name is Cadillac.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's a long story.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I need the next panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, David Dominguez, I believe, representing himself.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Vlad K-U-C-H-E-R.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: More letters is hard to make out, but Vlad.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Justin Bernstein.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Good handwriting.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sarah O'Brien, even better.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mike Streeter.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I say B plus with the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You want to take these?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, feel that sugar.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Come on.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Which way do, how did we start last time?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right, we're going to start this and go north.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So we got...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So we got one operating mic.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, just got to make sure the light is on.

chapters.summary: Streeter says he is a founding member of the New York Clean Air Collective and supports Intro 48. He argues existing law already exempts fuel pumps and processing devices and says industry claims about ignored exemption stickers are misleading.
chapters.title: Mike Streeter calls 561-A unfixable and corrects industry claims

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: My name is Mike Streeter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: I'm a founding member of the New York Clean Air Collective, but I'm speaking on my own behalf.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: I submit idling complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Let me just start off by saying intro 48, good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Please pass.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: It's long overdue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Intro 561A, unfixable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: And intro 11A, not necessary in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Regarding an earlier question from Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Epstein and to the NYSEC representative, it's shocking to me that some industry reps like NYSEC here are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: not aware that fuel pump vehicles are already exempt from idling restrictions when they are operating the pumps.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: DEP will reject any complaint for a vacuum truck, fuel truck, food oil truck, etc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: If there is even a possibility that work requiring the engine is taking place, period.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: End of story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: And to the rep from Interior Demo Contractors Association, most compacting trucks wait until they have enough bins to start compacting continuously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: That's how they avoid tickets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: We see.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: see it all the time and their operators can do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Also, there's no such thing as an exemption sticker that is being ignored, as someone brought up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: The stickers that DEP issues merely reflect the existing exemptions that a truck's equipment already enjoys under the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: And then regarding aggregate cement, I live near 3rd Ave and DeGraw in Brooklyn, which is where Thomas Green Playground is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Last year, aggregate cement trucks were there nearly every day with one and sometimes two big, loud trucks idling for hours on end.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: People live there, people work there, and kids play there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: The idling was incessant, and I'm shocked to hear anyone try to defend that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: There's no reason for trucks of that type to be idling that long away from the work site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: And guess what?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: They caught on, and they suddenly were able to shut off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: On that note, I...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: I wanted to talk about misinformation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, but I got to like, you know, we got tons of witnesses left and they got to get on with their lives.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I got to be at least close to the two minute thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, that was the gist of my discussion is misinformation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: There's a lot of misinformation out there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mike Streeter
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate your good testimony and your patience for waiting to deliver it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Bernstein says he was homeless in lower Manhattan and saw buses and trucks idling nonstop. He says the program changed driver behavior and urges the Council to reject 561-A.
chapters.title: Justin Bernstein shares homeless perspective and supports the complaint program

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I just want to introduce myself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: My name is Justin Bernstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I'm a participant of the Idling program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I was born and raised in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: As a Brooklyn native, I've always noticed there was a problem with trucks and buses idling, especially in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I always thought it was just part of life being in the big city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: My story is probably going to be a little bit different because I was homeless for quite some time in the lower Manhattan area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I saw firsthand how there would be buses and trucks of all sizes idling nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: You could not walk down Canal Street without seeing a fleet of coach-sized buses idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: There was really nothing you could do about it before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: There has always been a law against idling, but it was not enforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: This is the first of many examples that made me want to take action when I discovered the idling program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Once this program had begun, it did not take long before I noticed change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I saw firsthand how this program changed the driving habits of a lot of drivers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Companies were being held accountable, and through that accountability, change was being achieved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I am proud to say I have helped in this process and the opportunity the city gave every citizen to do what they can do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I am honored to work with all the good people involved to make this a positive change in this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I am just one New Yorker, and a lot of people besides myself have put in a ton of work into this project, and it would be soul-crushing for all of our hard work to be possibly tossed out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I believe there are tools available to make this program more efficient and easier for all parties involved.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Just being able to participate in this program helped me tremendously when there was no other opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I say no to 561 as we already have a lot of stipulations with refrigeration units, lift gates, buses picking up and dropping off active.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: processing devices and it uses all these excuses as trucks I see use these lift gates they turn them on and off to avoid

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: to reset basically reset the timer reset the clock so you would have to start your three minutes over again all these are already being used to abuse the system

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: I've seen this happen in the field.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: Once drivers are aware, they're able to cheat the system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Bernstein
utterances.text: From what I've seen, they will cheat the system.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your compelling testimony and personal history and life story.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're grateful to have you here today.

chapters.summary: Kucher says he grew up near the Coney Island wastewater plant and participates in the complaint program. He argues 561-A would benefit out-of-state polluters and that Intro 48 would expand community participation.
chapters.title: Vlad Kucher opposes 561-A and supports Intro 48

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: My name is Vlad Kachriavi, and I'm a participant of the Citizens Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: My concern for air quality started from a very young age, since the Coney Island wastewater treatment plant is right next to where I grew up, and it makes the smell of fecal matter every time the weather is nice outside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Imagine my enthusiasm when I discovered that I can be part of a program that seeks to reduce pollution and improve the quality of life for my neighborhood while getting rewarded for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: At Brooklyn College, I enrolled in a public health class where I learned that public health is primarily the responsibility of government, but a successful public health enterprise must involve all sectors of the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: And this is why I'm here today, to testify against proposals such as Intro 561A that undermine community efforts for the benefit of out-of-reach polluting

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: corporate entities and advocate for proposals like Intro 48 that extend opportunities to reduce pollution to New Yorkers in all boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Adopting the proposed Intro 5618 is detrimental.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Negligent companies would be given a pass at the expense of our neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: They complain that fines are unfair, but in my experience, what is unfair is these companies and their employees coming into our streets from their out-of-state headquarters and releasing air pollutants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: As they complete their work quotas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: The money that 561A will be saving these entities is not likely to be used to ameliorate their negligent practices, hence will not benefit our communities in any way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: The revenue that participants are rewarded as a result of the program is circulated back into our local economy, as it should.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: In the face of grim public health,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: of statistics on air pollution, the program has brought great benefits to our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: One of these is empowering of concerned citizens from all boroughs to seek fairness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Intro 48 serves this purpose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: As someone from a multicultural neighborhood, I can attest that those whose English is not their strong language are often the most exposed to environmental

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: hazards and the hardest working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: They deserve the opportunity to advocate for themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Please don't undermine this program with Intro 561A and instead look towards supporting the health and livelihoods of our communities by considering Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: I would like to end by saying that unlike polluting entities that are profiting from our neighborhoods that are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: advocating for this environmental program, are working towards improving the livelihoods of all New Yorkers, since we believe that everyone that works hard to keep the city running deserves clean air, even the employees of corporate polluters, even those in favor of 561A, and especially their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: So vote no for 561A and yes for 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Vlad Kucher
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, please state your name and commence with your testimony.

chapters.summary: O'Brien, a young Queens native, says she is at risk of lung cancer despite not smoking and that children face school-bus and truck exhaust. She opposes 561-A and says her Arabic-speaking mother cannot use the English-only portal.
chapters.title: Sarah O'Brien opposes 561-A and supports language access

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: My name is Sarah O'Brien.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: I'm 24 years old, a native New Yorker, raised in Queens, your district actually.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Grew up in Niche, went to public school my whole life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: I still live here and intend to stay here in this great city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: And being that I'm a proud New Yorker and believe I have a lot to live for, I try to take good care of my health within my means, you know, like exercise, eat well, manage stress.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: I don't drink and I certainly do not smoke.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: And despite that,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Being that I live in this city, I'm at risk of lung cancer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Why is it that 20% of lung cancer patients in this city have never smoked a cigarette in their life?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: This is why I'm ashamed to see Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Why would anyone propose such a bill that puts this amazing program at risk, a citizen-led program that has generated over 350,000 complaints, a program that has generated over $145 million in fines, and above all, protected public health?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Public health for every New Yorker from all walks of life.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: I was five years old in 2007, and I remember how much worse it was then before the program going to school in Queens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: And still, children of this city have to go to school and brace the exhaust from delivery trucks, construction vehicles, and their own school buses that sit in idle for hours on end.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Their fragile lungs cannot handle that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Why should they?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Because a truck or bus driver wants to take a nap, eat lunch, charge their phone, or run the heat?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: In New York City, children brace the cold to walk to school, bundled up in their puffers,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: And these grown men and women, they can't do the same.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Like, these grown men and women...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, take your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: These grown men and women who operate these vehicles can't do the same to stay warm and not pollute the air that we share.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: We need more people submitting complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: My mom, she speaks Arabic as her first language and wanted to participate in the program, but because the program is only available in English, she can't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: I mean,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Like from the DEP's testimony earlier, that's a joke that they say that they offer instructions in other languages because that's not the same as translating the portal.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah O'Brien
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says the program is working in some ways but not others and that the current iteration is not where the Council wants to land. He thanks the panel for personal testimony and moves to the next panel.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks panel and acknowledges program is not fully working

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, you know, it's your...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, the program is working, but in some aspects it's not.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, the current iteration of it is certainly not where we want to land.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But I appreciate the input of everyone on this panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I've learned so many things that...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So this is an iterative process.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so I want to appreciate everyone's good testimony and, you know, being here, sharing your testimony, personal stories.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It really helps, and I thank you for your patience for being here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But I've got to move on to the next panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: She comes with the blouse and everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: You know, shoot the thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, the next panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Luis Politano, best hand running so far.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Representing himself.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Dylan Stack, even better.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're killing it now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wanfang Wu, right up there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Gregory Gonzalez, B-.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oren Galchin?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, or in Galchen.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is kind of like pest fail.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'd like to welcome Sierra.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: She is...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sierra Townsend, she was in the audience, now she's here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the co-counsel to this committee.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What did I do last time?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Where did I go?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I started there?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I started there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, now I'm going to start this side.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I can never remember where I started or didn't start.

chapters.summary: Stack, vice president of the New York Clean Air Collective, says 25 civic groups oppose 561-A. He argues the bill would eliminate millions in penalties corporations should pay and urges the Council to pass Intro 48 instead.
chapters.title: Dylan Stack calls 561-A a corporate giveaway and unsalvageable

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Hello, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: My name is Dylan Stack.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: I'm the vice president of the New York Clean Air Collective, and I'm a New York City resident.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: I think the current count is 25 civic groups in New York City oppose Intro 561A, and I regretfully say that I believe it is unsalvageable as a piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: This bill would not do anything to improve the environment or the air quality of New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: This bill is a corporate giveaway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Amazon paid $9 million, as we saw in the news this year, because of their incessant idling that hasn't stopped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: If we have 561A passed with its provisions about regeneration and processing devices and everything else in that piece of legislation that is going to be debunked in the written testimony of this hearing,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: that is going to cause millions and millions of fines that these corporations should be paying to be gone forever.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Because this is about the air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: As we heard from Councilmember Aviles, 2,400 kids a year die from air pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: This is something that we all care about deeply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: And I think New York City should be a leader in clean air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: We do not need to go back.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You're looking at the...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Ultimate leader in New York City clean air.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I talked about what I did years ago, and I'm still doing, where in one fell swoop, I cobbled together a thing that created the equivalent of every car, truck, and bus being taken off the road forever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I'm not a slouch when it comes to

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's the clean air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I'll give you your time back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: You've been the committee chairman of this committee for 18 years, the Environmental Committee in the greatest city in the world, a leading city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: I think that we can be the shining example to the rest of the world about preserving the citizen air complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: We can pass intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: We can help environmental justice neighborhoods, the residents there submit the complaints in their own language.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, that would be up to the, you know, to the people who are.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Putting in the violations who aren't going to those neighborhoods as much as they go to other neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So that's for you to talk about with your other people participating in this good program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Where were the people out in the communities of color and the EJ communities?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This is like a Manhattan and like Brooklyn thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But anyway.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Now I'm testifying, and so I don't want to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You're here to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Thank you for your comments, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: I believe the city can lead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: The city can expand the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: I don't think we should go back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: The truck industry, I very much appreciate that they have been very successful over the years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: They can hire lobbyists to come here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: And testify on their behalf, I don't think the lobbyists fully understand the technology in these trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: That's why Intro 561A is so detrimental.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: It talks about regeneration, when they can regenerate while they're driving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: All these claims, like I mentioned,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: will be thoroughly debunked in the written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: So I would ask you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Chairman, I would ask the members of the council, I would ask the speaker to reconsider why are we going back with Intro 561?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: This would do nothing to help the environment.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, you know, this is what reconsideration looks like.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, reconsideration is a hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so, I mean, I'm not happy with where, this is why we, you know, I felt that after the, you know, last amendments were made, I thought that we could certainly do better, which is why we're here today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, I don't have to be here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I wanted to be here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I wanted to hear from everyone so that I could make it better.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, no one wants to make it better more than you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Dylan Stack
utterances.text: Chairman.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm not going to fight with anybody else.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It was just his turn, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: He looked like he could take it, too.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: He looks like a nice guy.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So, yes.

chapters.summary: Galshan says he grew up in Oklahoma and now supports New York's idling enforcement. He argues 561-A is a poison pill for Intro 11 and defends paying citizens for enforcement work.
chapters.title: Oren Galshan opposes 561-A and defends citizen enforcement incentives

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: My name is Oren Galchin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: I grew up in Oklahoma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: I'm the son of a meteorologist who researched climate change for many years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: I'm here to speak against Intro 561A, unsalvageable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: In what I wonder, coming from Oklahoma, which is the exact opposite, in one of the best and most progressive cities in the world, why are we discussing this bill?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: A bill clearly sponsored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: by big corporations, and it's written as a poison pill for Intro 11, because Intro 11, no matter how good or bad or high the fines in, won't be enforceable if Intro 561 is passed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: And I would like to address another elephant in the room, something we all know about, that some people are more concerned that the people who actually are fighting every day to keep our air clean are making too much money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: What do I say to all this?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: First of all, it's not me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: And second of all, I hope more people make even more money fighting for our air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: There is no barrier to entry in our idle enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: The people most actively involved seem to be the only ones going on TV, doing town halls, and keeping active social media to alert and try and get other people to join.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Would we be saying...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: the same thing if there was a similar way to enforce crime tips.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: How about tax evasion?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Actually, we do pay people to enforce that, and I'm sure we all want people to get paid more to enforce that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: How about the red light cameras, as someone says, and the speeding cameras?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Do they make too much money?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Should we end them?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: These are all successful programs that have survived the test of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: And let's not forget with idling enforcement, 30% of the work goes unpaid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: I think I heard 40% since 40% of the tickets aren't even paid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: The remainder that does get paid, the city keeps 75% of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: That's more money for schools, parks, and to close our city's deficits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: Idling enforcement has become such a successful program because of the incredible people that are committed to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: They're up at 6.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: They go out till midnight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: They work weekends.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: They have jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: It can be 20 degrees outside, snow, rain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: They keep going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Oren Galshan
utterances.text: One thing I'll add, they're so lucky that they even got their faces and names printed in the New York Post.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Spirited.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I like that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, we can't do the clap thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, it's just the sergeant's old.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You're supposed to do this.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

chapters.summary: Wu says 561-A would stop self-prosecution by reducing awards and imposing short deadlines. She also warns that Intro 562's liability transfer could let last-mile contractors close and reopen to avoid tickets.
chapters.title: Wan Fang Wu opposes 561-A, 11, and 562 and supports 48

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: My name is Wan Fang Wu.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: I oppose all of the bills except for Intro 48, which expands access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: I believe Intro 11 is going to destroy small businesses with unbearable fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Intro 561.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: One will stop participation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: I don't think it's salvageable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Right now, it takes the DEP, as we are aware, one year to issue a ticket, which is bad for everybody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: That backlog is finally starting to taper off as more citizens are helping out with the prosecutions by prosecuting themselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Because currently, if the DEP takes no action for 45 days, we can prosecute the complaint ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: And I should do mine within 30 days when DEP gives me the green light.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: However, 561 stops this in two ways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: First, it makes it so that if you self-prosecute the extra $25, it's going to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Basically disincentivize this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: We have to show up for the oath hearings and participate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: And we don't know when oath is going to call us on the day of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: So that makes it no longer worthwhile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: There's also a 30-day term to issue this if you go the self-prosecution route.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: However, it can take the DEP up to two months to process this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: They say that they don't have proper printer access for some special forms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: So 561 removes this pressure release valve that addresses a lot of the problems, such as this big backlog.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: I also want to comment on Intro 562's transfer liability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: I think

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: That's a big loophole because if we let Amazon and other big companies try to pass this on to their last mile contractors, those contractors and outfits, they can just ignore the ticket, close up shop, and then

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Wan Fang Wu
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As if that matters.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, you made a lot of really good points in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, Josh, after this panel is complete, Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wu, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you could, you know, meet with my legislative director out in the hall and just give him, you know, like a...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Further download on the points that you made.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, because yours was a very compelling testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I want to make sure we get every drop of nectar sort of out of it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Gonzalez says he has driven diesel trucks and operated heavy equipment and knows the health effects of exhaust. He says the complaint program pushed armored-car companies to switch to electric vehicles and urges rejection of 561-A.
chapters.title: Gregory Gonzalez opposes 561-A and cites fleet electrification

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Gregory Gonzalez, and I'm here in opposition of 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Intro 561A aims to diminish and destroy the Citizens Air Complaint Program, which has been one of New Yorkers'most effective tools in combating unnecessary truck and bus idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: 561A hinders the DEP's ability to pursue air complaints and reduces incentives for citizens to take part in the air complaint program at a time when I believe we really need more participation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: For me, a concerning part of 561A is that it opens a loophole for diesel vehicles to avoid fines and idle indefinitely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Diesel vehicles are some of the worst polluters in New York City, and I've seen that firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I've driven diesel engine trucks, and I've operated heavy equipment before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I've laid asphalt.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I'm not a person who works in a corporate office of a bus company or trucking concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I know what it's like to have to work next to large diesel vehicles all day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I know that the exhaust tears up your lungs and that when you come over the end of the day, you have a headache and a sore throat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Getting trucks to stop idling is not only good for New Yorkers, but it's especially good for the people who are operating the trucks, the buses, and the heavy equipment that are polluting the air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Idling is unnecessary and it hurts New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I would like to speak on what I have personally observed on the streets of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: I've watched the Citizens Air Complaint Program work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: When you submit complaints through the Citizens Air Complaint Program, companies actually take notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: We are starting to see companies change their fleet vehicles from combustion engines to electric vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: The armored truck companies, Ferrari Express, Loomis, Malka, Amit, have been some of the worst polluters in Manhattan, especially in the Diamond District.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: And I would observe them idling in Midtown for hours in the same spots over and over again, day after day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: After receiving complaints, they begin to change their vehicles to electric vehicles.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: There's now notable difference in the air quality in these areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gregory Gonzalez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes.

chapters.summary: Politano says he has submitted nearly 4,000 complaints since 2022. He warns that the regeneration exemption and 60-day deadline would wipe out enforcement and that requiring citizens to prosecute would burden environmental justice neighborhoods.
chapters.title: Luis Politano opposes 561-A and warns of lost complaints

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Hello, hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: My name is Luis Palatano.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I've been an active participant of the Citizens Air Complaint Program since April 2022 and have submitted nearly 4,000 complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I am present today to testify against the provisions outlined in Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: First, the diesel engine regeneration exemption will create a loophole rendering the anti-idling law hamstrung.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I learned earlier that the problem is the average person and the DEP reviewer has no idea the truck is in regeneration mode.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I suppose a solution to that problem would be to have an exterior indicator.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Let someone outside the truck or someone viewing the video, let them know that the truck's in regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Second, the 60-day expiration of pending violations will allow polluters to avoid accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Because the DEP is understaffed and the oath is understaffed, this deadline will delete tens of thousands of complaints and wipe out millions in city revenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: If you're going to impose a 60-day expiration, you're going to have to hire more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: People and DEP and oath.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: And last, forcing everyday citizens to become legal prosecutors to defend clear video evidence will create barriers for low-income environmental justice neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I live and reside in southeastern Queens, which is home to several environmental justice neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I actually operate in Jamaica, just south, adjacent to your district, south of Hillside, down to Liberty, to 110th Street, to 180th Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: If this passes, this can make my job very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: It doesn't do a lot of the work I've done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I've made impact in many different areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: I can say very specific locations where they don't run their engines anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: If I don't make up, keep up my appearances, it's going to reverse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: The CHCP is successfully curbing pollution and held polluters accountable at no cost to the taxpayer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Luis Politano
utterances.text: Okay, I urge this committee to protect public health and vote no on 561A.

chapters.title: Gennaro thanks panel and calls next panel
