chapters.summary: An unnamed lifelong New Yorker says 561-A would dismantle the complaint program and give truck owners loopholes. He praises Gennaro's Tobacco 21 law and asks him to stand up to industry again by withdrawing 561-A.
chapters.title: Lifelong New Yorker urges rejection of 561-A and cites Tobacco 21

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Testing one, two, three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Yep, I think we're good.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Good afternoon, council members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I want to thank each one of you for everything that you guys do for New York City, both seen and unseen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Each one of you have my deepest respect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: As a lifelong New Yorker, I am here today to urge you to reject Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This bill does not fix, reform, or improve the program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Instead, it will dismantle it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It provides truck owners with loopholes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: That will allow them to idle with impunity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: I want to focus on two specific items.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: First, diesel regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Unfortunately, diesel regeneration cannot be seen, not by the person filming it, not by the DEP inspector, and not by the hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: officer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The moment this bill passes, every diesel truck, every bus driver in New York will have a permanent and unverifiable excuse to idle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Every idling ticket becomes unprovable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Second, the 60-day clock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: DEP has 60 days to make it happen, or else they could walk away from the complaint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: This deadline is not ambition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It will prove to be impossible and untenable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: With this bill, tens and thousands of valid complaints filed in good faith will be expired, unreviewed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: The 60-day clock does not speed up enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It guarantees that nearly every complaint expires unresolved and violators will walk away scot-free.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: And finally, I want to speak directly to the main sponsor of this bill, Chairman Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Your record is not in question here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: It is this reason that this moment matters.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You've authored 50 laws to protect citizens of this great city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You wrote Tobacco 21, Raising the Age of the Tobacco E-Cig Buyers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: New England Journal of Medicine said this saved countless lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: You accomplished this by standing up to a powerful industry, an industry that insisted that life as usual

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: and that the status quo was okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: At the end of the day, you were right and they were wrong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: What we ask in terms of this program, this is the first tool that truly held the biggest polluters accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Ladies and gentlemen, we are asking you to do it again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Don't cave in to big corporations, the trucking companies, the lobbyists, and their respective unions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: We ask you to stay the course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Do what's right, as you have done before.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Withdraw this bill and save lives again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says Tobacco 21 took eight years and was opposed by major health groups before it became national policy. He says the episode shows the value of standing up to powerful industries.
chapters.title: Gennaro recounts eight-year fight to pass Tobacco 21

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I do appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just need a...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know we have to move along, but you mentioned Tobacco 21.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I started Tobacco 21 in 2005, and it took us eight years to get it done.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: By 2013 when I was term limited out the first time, right at the end, we got it in and we got it passed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the reason why it took eight years to get it passed because it was adamantly opposed, raising the age to buy cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It was adamantly opposed by the American Lung Association and the American Cancer Society.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: They testified vehemently against it, saying that raising the age would make tobacco more taboo and therefore more alluring for people to have because it was, like, forbidden.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Because no one else had done it, so we had no data to work off.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I worked with those organizations, and no one would go for it because, like, you know, these big health entities were against the bill.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I said, look, well, let's just try it for, like, a year or two, and then if the data comes back bad and smoking goes up, we'll sunset the bill, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: They didn't want to go for that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so we got it passed over their opposition.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then the data started pouring in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Teen smoking rates plummeted.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then every jurisdiction in the country went to school on us on that it really was a good idea to do that in 2000.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, 2020 it became, passed in 2013, became national policy, you know, federal policy in 2020.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And the only shame is that the fact that had we done it eight years earlier, so many more lives would have been saved.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yale recently did a study saying over the next X number of years,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It would save like another 500,000 lives.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so that was a good bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: If I may, just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public
utterances.text: Diesel fumes are the tobacco of New York City streets today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Profound.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Profound.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Let me just have a sidebar with counsel for a second before I go to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just, that's why I have a council.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sometimes I have to be counseled, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So, thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please, the next witness.

chapters.summary: Goman says she lives uptown with her children and has seen less idling because of the complaint program. She opposes 561-A's 60-day and 14-day limits and supports Intro 48's language access.
chapters.title: Irina Goman opposes 561-A and supports Intro 48

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: My name is Irina Goman, and I live with my children uptown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: I'm here because I know firsthand how the citizen air complaint program is making the air quality better in Upper Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: My family and I noticed that fewer trucks and buses idle than they used to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: We cannot go backwards on clean air in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: We have come too far.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Unfortunately, if this package of bill passes, I fear that New York's air will get dirtier.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: I'm especially troubled by Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: This bill will prohibit the DEP from issuing violations more than 60 days after a citizen complaint is submitted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: And it gives New Yorkers who are full-time workers, full-time caregivers, or disabled only 14 days to file a complaint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: This is a terrible idea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Imagine if building owners could create an unsafe fire or ventilation situations, and then the DOB was barred from issuing citations if they found out too late, even if they had bulletproof video evidence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Allow me to speak about Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: As you may be able to tell, English is not my first language.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: I am fortunate to be extremely comfortable in English, but many New Yorkers who were born abroad are not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Intro 48 corrects the unfair policy that kept those New Yorkers from having full access to the air complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: These New Yorkers will not be able to report idling trucks and buses, drywall dust, and some other construction violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Language access is a necessary step in improving the air complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: The rest of this bill will make this program more confusing and out of reach for everyday New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: The program should be fair and more efficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Let it be clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: The council cannot pass intro 561A, which will make pollution worse in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: The chair talked about the balance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: But you can't have a balance that includes more dirty air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Just the last.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Note that I think that nothing changed behavior quite as effectively as a fine that hits your wallet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Irina Goman
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gennaro apologizes as a phone alarm interrupts the hearing and says he needs to take medication. He then calls the next witness, Grant, to testify.
chapters.title: Gennaro handles phone alarm and calls Grant

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, by the way, hang on.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So these alarms that have been going off.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: My phone can't ring, but alarms will go off, so I have to...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Grant says DEP is already far beyond 60 days and that the bill could toss out a year of complaints. He also warns that broadening processing devices to electrical equipment could let almost any engine use qualify.
chapters.title: Grant critiques 60-day deadline and broad processing-device definition

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: Good afternoon, all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify on intros 561A11 and general oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: My name is Grant, and I'm a citizen complainant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: A few of the specific concerns.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: One is around the 60 days, which I think has been brought up before, but DP is currently well beyond the 60-day timeline and is almost up to a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: And so I think the bill as written currently could be construed to wind up throwing out a bunch of complaints from the past year or more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: I think that the goal, as has been discussed in the hearing previously, of speeding up processing and issuing notices of violation in a more timely manner is noble and is well-intentioned, but that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: forcing a timeline on DEP, enforcing them to toss complaints if that timeline is not hit, I think would need some type of...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: continuity, like how do we get from our current backlog to that steady state.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: One other comment I'll provide is around the definition of the processing device, which has gotten a lot of discussion around

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: certain vehicles needing to run the engine as to dispense fuel or compact or whatnot,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: which is that the definition as is written right now is fairly expansive and contemplates these various

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: situations where if the vehicle is using a mechanical connection to perform work that is allowed and I think Oath and Oath Appeals has considered these situations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: I think one concern around broadening the definition to include electrical equipment that's necessary for work is

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: that it's very broad and could be almost anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: Like if someone is charging their phone to get a text from their boss, well, their boss is a necessary part of their work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: Their phone's a necessary part of their work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: So I think you could see complaints or summonses dismissed for that reason, which I think is probably not intended.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just finish your thought.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Grant
utterances.text: I think that's probably not what the committee is intending to do is, you know, allow Eileen to charge people's phones.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says many witnesses interpreted the 60-day section as throwing out violations, but that is not the intent. He says the language will be clarified so it does not produce that result.
chapters.title: Gennaro clarifies that 60-day provision is not intended to void complaints

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And here's what I'm going to do.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Well, let me just talk to the council and the committee first because she's the one that's going to have to do it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to do this.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Many people have testified that once the 60-day window at DEP is up, like all these violations get thrown out.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That is an interpretation of that section, but that is not the intent of the section.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so we'll be more clear that that is not going to be the manifestation of that section.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I just wanted to put that on the record that while people are in turmoil,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: interpreting it that way.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's not the intent and the way, but it's helpful to hear from people who have that interpretation that only

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: makes it clear to me that that has to be made more clear, that that is not going to be the result of

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: of that section.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, a lot of things are going to get changed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so I just...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I would have liked it better if she had done that, you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But she's not supposed to, so it's just like I had to do it, you know?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So anyway, but they had it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So, you know, just the fact that so many people are interpreting it that way makes it, you know, all the more clear that it has to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So that's not...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What people take away from it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I wasn't mad.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I did it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I did it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

chapters.summary: Duke says the complaint program empowers residents to hold large corporations accountable. He opposes 561-A's regeneration exemption and 60-day window and warns that 11-A's penalties could devastate small businesses.
chapters.title: Duke opposes 561-A and warns 11-A would hurt small businesses

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: My name is Duke.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: I moved to New York a few years ago, and I personally witnessed the success of the Citizen Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: The program empowers everyday New Yorkers to hold major corporations like Amazon, Verizon, and Con Edison accountable for illegal idling, and it gives citizens a voice in protecting our air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Intro 561A threatened this progress.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: First, the proposed diesel regeneration exemption could create a loophole that is extremely difficult to verify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Second, the 60-day window you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: The third one, reducing incentives would discourage participation and weaken enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Instead, we should help DDP process complaints more efficiently, not making citizen enforcement more difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: I'm also concerned about Intro 11, which would increase idling penalty to as much as $7,500.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: While support strong enforcement against repeat offenders, such penalty could be financially devastating for small businesses and independent contractors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: We need strong enforcement, but we also need fairness and proportionality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: The real problem is illegal ID.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: not the citizens who report it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: I respectfully urge the council to reconsider both bills and preserve the effectiveness of the citizen air complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Thanks for your time.

chapters.summary: Gennaro thanks the panel and says their input is noted. He calls the next panel of Ting Ting Wong, Haxel Rios, Peder Wessel, Robin Warren, and Adam Tomlinson.
chapters.title: Gennaro thanks panel and calls next panel

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You've waited a long time to say that, and I appreciate the input.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, it's duly noted and greatly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I want to thank this panel very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And we're going to call the next panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next panel looks like Ting Ting, first name.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Wong, maybe?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Haxel Rios with handwriting so crisp it looks like it was typed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: First name P-E-D-E-R, Wessel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Robin Warren.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Adam.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Tomlinson?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Last.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know what?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I started this side last time, but the microphone's already there, so just start in this way and we'll work that way.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Just state your name for the record and proceed.

chapters.summary: Wong says she is a former substitute teacher and former complaint participant. She argues 561-A would exempt school buses and weaken enforcement, and she urges the Council to reject it and improve the program instead.
chapters.title: Ting Ting Wong opposes 561-A and describes school-bus idling concerns

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Hello, my name is Ting Ting Wong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: I am a resident of Bed-Stuy and a former participant in the error complaint program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairman Gennaro, for your considerable patience and attention today.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hey, this is...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I get paid to be here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You don't, you know?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: But still, I really appreciate you taking the time to hear everyone's testimony and your dedication to protecting clean air.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: I first learned about the air complaint program when I was a substitute teacher in New York City public schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Students spend a lot of time outdoors, and the difference in air quality on a playground is noticeable when a large truck, especially one that is idling, is nearby.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: More than 15 years ago, the city council wisely restricted idling near schools to one minute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: The council specifically cited school buses whose emissions are especially harmful because of exemptions under New York state law dating back to the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Intro 561A would effectively

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: school buses from enforcement in many circumstances on the grounds that they need to run their engines to maintain heating or cooling for the very students whose health they are putting at risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: DEP standards for evidence are already demanding, and in practice they are much stricter than the law itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Videos submitted by first-time participants are often rejected, as are submissions from experienced participants when there is any doubt or deficiency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: This happened to me, and it's why I don't really participate in the program anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: DEP provides little guidance, and I was fortunate that other participants volunteered their time to help me get over the learning curve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Enforcement in one neighborhood also helps discourage idling in others.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: DEP needs more resources to work through its backlog of complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Respondents should receive summonses more quickly or at least receive warning notices with links to the videos in question.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: This is only fair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: We have already heard several proposals for accomplishing this without changing the law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: I urge council to reject 561A and focus on improving the program for more participation.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We appreciate you being here and your patience.

chapters.summary: Warren says she is a mother of school-aged children and discovered the complaint program while managing her daughter's asthma. She argues 561-A creates an unverifiable regeneration loophole and an unworkable 60-day deadline.
chapters.title: Robin Warren opposes 561-A and describes daughter's asthma

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: My name is Robin Warren.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: I am a New York City resident and a mother of two school-aged children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: I'm here to respectfully urge you to reject Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: It is deeply exhausting to watch the steady erosion of common sense protections that keep our communities safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Around the country, we are seeing bedrock environmental laws weakened, vital scientific research sidelined, and basic public safety measures scaled back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Today, this council faces a defining choice to replicate that pattern of erosion or to use its power to preserve what keeps us safe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Our family discovered the Citizens Air Complaint Program through the New York Times, out of sheer desperation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: As my husband, a naturalized U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Citizen from Kolkata, India, and I struggled to manage our young daughter's acute asthma, we know firsthand that this program works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: For decades, anti-idling laws went unenforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: The Citizens Air Complaint Program changed everything, empowering everyday citizens to hold commercial polluters accountable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: The city's own data shows that New York idlers waste over $28 million in fuel every single year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: While commercial fleets make up just 6% of our traffic, they generate over half of our dangerous tailpipe pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: This program is the only real shield our neighborhoods have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Intro 561A breaks what is working.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: It creates an unverifiable loophole that lets diesel trucks idle indefinitely, while slapping an unworkable 60-day deadline on a backlogged agency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: This opens the door for the city to dismiss 170,000 pending violations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: And lets commercial polluters off scot-free.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It really doesn't.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We've been through that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: The corporate...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Your time is, you know, like your time is completed.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Robin Warren
utterances.text: Thank you for listening, sir.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You bet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Can I take this, please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ting Ting Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Tomlinson says he walks past the same idling trucks every day near schools, museums, and parks. He says drivers often turn engines off only briefly and urges the Council to amplify rather than restrict the program.
chapters.title: Adam Tomlinson opposes 561-A and describes daily truck idling

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Chairman, Committee Council, thank you for the time this afternoon to discuss this bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: I contest Bill 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: On my way into work every day, I walk past schools, museums, buildings, parks, same trucks every day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Half an hour earlier, same truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Half an hour later, same truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: High capacity engines, diesel running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: You know, I'm the sort of guy, as you can imagine, I will knock on the window and let them know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: And I don't mind the response that I get.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: They will turn it off, smile, I walk 10 paces on, and they smile and turn it back on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Or they'll move slightly just to make sure and they'll chastise me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Like I'm trying to be a representative member of my community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: I'm thinking about the children, the elderly and the vulnerable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: And these guys, they just think it's a joke.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: It's not a joke.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: So I really appreciate some of the reporting that our community has done, the movements that have happened to press on these people that don't take this environment seriously.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: You know, they know exactly what they're doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: They shouldn't be doing it, and they do it anyway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: We walked by two cars down on the way here that we're doing outside the park here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: It's 65 degrees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: It's beautiful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Open the window, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: You can smell the exhaust as you walk by.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: You know, these children, elderly people, people with health conditions, they simply want to go about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: in their lives and they can't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: They can't have that wonderful environment that we expect for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: I find this especially infuriating because my wife and I are expecting in February and I feel it's my obligation to come here and say we need to lean on the Mahada and I don't feel the bill really extends the impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: I think it restricts the impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: But there has been some really good feedback, and thank you so much for your clarification that we won't be six months and chopping off, because I think that should be held.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Anyway, I think it's a great program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: It should be amplified rather than restricted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Thank you for your time today and to help us motivate drivers to do the right thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for being here, and congratulations to you and your wife.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, his name is on the paper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Yeah, I got dyslexic handwriting, so that's an F minus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's your name?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Adam Thomas.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Adam, Adam, yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Adam, yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: There you go.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And if you want to see SUVs idling,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You should go to City Hall parking lot and see all the SUVs for like the deputy mayors that are sitting there idling and idling and idling and idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Adam Tomlinson
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be a good choice to amplify the program to include those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just saying it's something that I...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

chapters.summary: Wessel says he works in tech and suggests DEP could send automated email, text, or mail notices with video links as soon as complaints arrive. He argues this would reduce the year-long delay without changing the law.
chapters.title: Peder Wessel proposes automated notices and video access for fleets

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: My name is Peter Wessel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Thank everyone here for being patient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I had planned a different testimony, but I want to react to some of the things I've heard over the last four hours at this point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I keep hearing that we're saying status quo is not going to work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: And someone was asking before, well, what is broken?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: And the response back was something along the line of, we asked the questions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I don't know what's broken.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Clearly, there's too much idling happening.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I think we can all agree to that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I heard when I listened to the respondents from the trucking and the busing industry, they clearly want to have notifications much faster.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I couldn't agree anymore.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: And I think there's opportunities to improve that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I don't think DP is here today, but maybe the feedback can be provided.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I work in tech, and at least to my knowledge, there are other agencies in the city already taking proactive action to notify participants of programs if something is wrong.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I've seen it to do it in the housing that like something has been complained about a housing lord you can get notification before they do an audit on it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I think all the information is needed for DEP to give fast, rapid, accurate information to a respondent is in the claim that's been made by a citizen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You have the truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You have the license plates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You have the point of where it's been observed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You have the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: The video files are there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You can go to the portal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You can click it in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I get that's hard for a respondent to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: All that information is there.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You could send an auto message out to those who'd like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: opted in to say, hey, do you want an e-notification?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: We'll send you an email, maybe an SMS, whatever you want to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You can get an opted-in message that's like on the day, someone here was wearing a mask saying delivery on the day, RDS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: This would be the same thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You get your message delivered on the day, no reminder needed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Here's the information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: If you haven't opted in, I could imagine a world where you say, we don't know your email, we don't know your phone number, but we have your address because it's on your truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Send them a message in the mail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Hey, we received this information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: If you want to know more, go in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: Then the timeline is gone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: It's no longer a year and a half until I found out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You can take the cure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I actually think, frankly speaking, with the information at hand,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: If you just look at the amount of tickets that are happening, if you're an operator of a fleet, just ask your staff always to turn the engine off when they get to the destination.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: You will have nothing in the mail, no SMS is coming.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peder Wessel
utterances.text: I thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says the hearing has shown that the program is too analog and needs more technology. He notes that the mayor controls DEP staffing levels and that the Council cannot simply add staff on its own.
chapters.title: Gennaro agrees the program needs more technology and DEP staffing

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, this whole thing is like very analog.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so, you know, tech is required.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, I wish I could wave a magic wand and give DEP more staff.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I can't do that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, the mayor sets the staffing level for DEP.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, and I was saying the fact that, you know, some of the testimony is repetitive.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, everyone has their own, like, little slant on it that, you know, gives me better insight into which way.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We should go.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And this panel was very good in that regard.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I appreciate you being here and your patience and waiting to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you all very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Duke

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
