chapters.summary: Bisker says he is a former delivery driver and longtime complaint participant with asthma. He argues 561-A rewards polluters for gumming up the system and punishes citizens for participating, and he urges the Council to kill the bill.
chapters.title: Josh Bisker opposes 561-A and warns it ruptures public trust

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Thank you for being here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I'm dedicating my testimony to my beloved neighbor, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Pam Bino, who is permanently disabled from the asthma that she developed after moving here from Barbados.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: My name is Josh Bisker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I'm a former delivery driver, a longtime participant in the Citizens Air Complaint Program, and a born New Yorker who has had asthma since childhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I have the expertise to comment on today's bills, and their stakes are deeply personal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Intro 561A will effectively destroy the Citizens Air Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: It will protect corporate polluters with legal loopholes, hamper city agencies from holding them accountable, disincentivize public participation, and possibly retroactively void a vast number of outstanding complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I studied behavioral economics.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, we did the void complaints thing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know, I know, I know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I'm sticking to my...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I studied behavioral economics in urban planning at Hunter College, so I understand that the current air complaint program ingeniously pairs up two financial incentive mechanisms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Penalties for idling get corporations to stop polluting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Rewards from those penalties get members of the public to contribute complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: 561A throws a wrench into both mechanisms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: It effectively rewards polluters for having polluted so much that they gummed up the system and punishes citizens for having participated so avidly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: The lesson is that more polluting wins more allowances.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: for polluting, yet more participation is a waste of the public's time and effort.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: 561A encourages polluting and ruptures the public's trust in our government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: All future city programs asking the public to participate in oversight will suffer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: And in the meantime, the city, possibly, forfeits tens of millions of dollars in corporate environmental fees.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I once felt hopeless about the FedEx trucks that idled on my block every day, spewing out toxic fumes onto our stoops.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Then the idling program empowered me to fight back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I've seen the difference every day for years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Better air for my neighborhood, better health for my neighbors, and a chance to sit outside with Miss Pam.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Now, Inter 561 and its fellows 11, 562, 869 promise to end all of that, put these bills to bed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: I'm really grateful for your interest in ending air pollution by improving the idling program, but I'm here to tell you that only 48 of today's docket will do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Bisker
utterances.text: Kill this bill and its cousins forever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for your compelling testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You bet.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness.

chapters.summary: Dr. Eisenberg says he worked in New York City Department of Health clinics for many years. He describes idling pollutants' links to asthma, heart attacks, strokes, dementia, diabetes, and pregnancy complications, and opposes 561-A.
chapters.title: Dr. Seth Eisenberg opposes 561-A on public-health grounds

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Yeah, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: My name is Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Seth Eisenberg, and I've spent many years on the front lines working for New York City Department of Health clinics.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: I'm here today, again, to voice my strong opposition to Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: And I also thank the many other doctors, such as those of the New York Clinicians for Climate Action, who are likewise voicing their strong opposition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: doctor for over 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: I'm concerned about the adverse health effects of idling exhaust, and I really admire how the Citizens Air complaint program has been reducing idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Vehicle idling releases a concentrated mix of toxic pollutants, including fine particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: and even volatile organic compounds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Nitrogen oxides and particulate matter severely irritate the airways, causing increased rates of asthma, emphysema, and lung cancer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: The fine particles easily cross into the bloodstream, promoting arterial plaque buildup and directly triggering heart attacks and strokes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Sustained exposure to idling fumes are associated with faster brain aging and increased risks of dementia and Parkinson's disease, as well as depression and anxiety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Even exposure during early childhood is linked to brain inflammation with reduced cognitive function, lower memory and IQ scores.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: And behavioral issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Idling air pollution contributes to insulin resistance, increasing the risk of developing diabetes and obesity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Idling fumes lower fertility, even by damaging sperm DNA and reducing ovarian reserves.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: And in my opinion, worst of all, even in pregnancy,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Idling exhaust increases the risk of miscarriage and highly problematic premature birth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Now, every big company with trucks in New York City is...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: is currently aware of the Citizens Air Complaint Program, and many are taking action to reduce idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: For example, as you've heard, Amazon has been the third worst idling violator with over 12,000 tickets.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please summarize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: I started recording idling violations six months ago, and not a single one of them is an Amazon vehicle, and I give all the credit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Seth Eisenberg
utterances.text: To the air complaint program.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for your good work, doctor.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Eisenberg, an attorney, argues 561-A's literal language is the problem and cannot be fixed by statements of intent. He says DEP needs more resources, not a law change, and disputes claims that the program is poorly targeted.
chapters.title: Eric Eisenberg says 561-A is unfixable and the status quo works

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Hi, I'm Eric Eisenberg, a local attorney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: This is not a hard problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: There is no problem, not a legislative one anyways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: And Intro 561A is unresurrectably, unfixably broken, as explained in detail by dozens of local and national organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: It can't be fixed with off-the-cuff statements of intent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Its literal, unambiguous language is the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: The status quo is working extremely well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: DEP just needs more resources to process complaints and process them quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: The program generates net revenue for the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: There is no net cost to fund it properly and speed up issuance of summons and notice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: We have raised this issue at every environmental budget hearing, yet DEP's idling unit still needs more workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: You can do it today, Chairman Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I can't.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Again, every time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I mean, I can't give DEP more staff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: You and Mamdani are not going to agree to give them more resources?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I don't talk to Mayor Mamdani, and so, you know, directly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: He talks with Donald Trump, so.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm just saying, you know, we're the legislature, the executive is the executive, and when the executive, you know,

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: we have the preliminary budget, then we say we need more DEP workers, and then they do the exec budget, and then.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It's very hard to get them to put more personnel in.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so we try, but at the end of the day, we negotiate and we get what we get.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We control the legislative side, but the executive side and preempting mayoral authority, we just don't have.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And you as an attorney, I'm sure, know that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Well, maybe I'm naive, but I believe in you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: The program itself, the Citizen Air Complaint Program, works brilliantly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: It is a false narrative propagated by Eric Adams'corrupt administration that the Citizen Complaint Program is not well geographically targeted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: We have charts and maps showing an amazing, near-perfect correlation between where the most pollution is and where the most reported violations occur.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: We will provide this data in our written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: As to Mr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Zogby's claim, DEP doesn't issue repeat violations until the prior violations have been adjudicated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Any defaults can be easily reopened.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: There are claims floating around.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: that the engine is necessary to run generators and lift gates and refrigeration units.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: But generators don't use engine power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: They create their own power.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: And actually using the engine to run lift gates and refrigeration units already provides an absolute defense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Certified Clean Idle is not clean.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Even in California, you can't run those engines near residential areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: And as a board member of the New York Clean Air Collective, I am proud of the standards that those submitting complaints have held themselves to.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Hundreds of thousands of complaints issued, and the current administration did not identify a single instance of misconduct in their paper.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: There's no problem that needs solving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: I think we're in agreement.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to, I mean, I know I took up some of your time, but I think I've, okay, finish your thought.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: I'm on my last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: I think we are in agreement that the current 561A is unworkable and its recent amendments have only made it worse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Will you commit that?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Should you not do the correct thing and withdraw this harmful bill, that the public get to weigh in on your amendments at a further hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I don't answer questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I take testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: You ask the questions, you kill the New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Eric Eisenberg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, it's like we don't answer questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's no committee council chair would ever do that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: doing this.

chapters.summary: Robidoux holds up his daughter's albuterol inhaler and says she has asthma. He argues 561-A would take away the complaint program that lets parents fight back against truck fumes and urges support for Intro 48.
chapters.title: Jonathan Robidoux opposes 561-A and shares daughter's asthma inhaler

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Hi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: My name is Jonathan Robidoux.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I'm here to speak against Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I have three young daughters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: My oldest daughter, Clementine, has asthma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: This is one of her albuterol inhalers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: As an asthma sufferer yourself, Chair, I'm sure you recognize this.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, I got my inhaler with me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: She needs this inhaler every day to get through either field hockey practice or dance class.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I can't describe how horrified and helpless it makes you feel to have your child tell you that they can't breathe or that it hurts to breathe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: An estimated 60,000 children attending New York City public schools have active asthma that may require an inhaler.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: You wouldn't believe how hard it was to get Aetna to cover this thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I spent a lot of time on the phone with them to get this covered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: That means there are over 100,000 parents in the city today worrying about how their child is going to breathe and how they are going to pay for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Every day in the city, I find trucks idling in excess of three minutes for no reason, and I report them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Everybody knows that vehicle emissions contribute to childhood asthma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: These trucks are choking our children with their fumes, and the Citizens Idling Complaint Program gives us a way to fight back and make a positive difference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Intro 561-A will take that away and tell all those parents that they and their children don't matter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: It cynically discourages and punishes participation in the idling program, just as Intro 48 hopes to foster it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Intro 48.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: would help expand the program to environmental justice communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: In my view, for these reasons, and because of the various loopholes 561 creates, I believe that it is unsalvageable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I just wanted to also make clear that, like he said too, nobody is getting a repeat offense before a first offense is adjudicated.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That's not actually true.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So if you have a situation where the violation happens and then the thing gets sent to the wrong address and then it's sort of like a default thing, the person doesn't show up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I guess what I mean is if I'm...

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I'm just saying that there are occasions where that does happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: And they can reopen it and re-adjudicate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: But I just wanted to make really just clear, like, if I went out there now and I got the same truck, like, three times on my way to the subway, like, was moving down the block.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: When DEP would issue, got around to those, issued those three summons from today, they would all be first offenses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: It would not be like one, two, three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I just wanted to.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, it's a fair point.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Fair point for sure.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you don't mind, can I share something with you that, you know, my own daughter that has asthma, whatever, she had difficulty, you know, I have one.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So I have the ability to, like, take the big breath or whatever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But you know these little tube things that you...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so then they can just draw it in slowly, and it's a lot easier for kids to do that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It doesn't cost a lot of money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: She gets it on her tongue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: You know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You get, it's this little, you hook that thing into the tube.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then she's at the other end of it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And then she just kind of like breathe normally.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And you get like, you know, it goes like deep into the lungs.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Because if she just, you're just going to get it like up here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: She's still like kind of getting used to it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: And trying different ways.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I would recommend this tube thing, you know.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so any pulmonologist would know that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: No, yeah.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: It worked a lot.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, it worked really well for my daughter.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Hope you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I just thought I'd mention that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, of course.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jonathan Robidoux
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please.

chapters.summary: Jacobs, a public-school teacher in the Bronx, says his students suffer asthma and smell exhaust in class. He argues 561-A would give corporate polluters a free pass and urges the Council to pass Intro 48 instead.
chapters.title: Aaron Jacobs opposes 561-A and supports Intro 48

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I'm a teacher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I don't have to be that loud, but I'll use the mic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: My name is Aaron Jacobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I've been a New York City public school teacher for the past 16 years, and I live in Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I teach ninth grade in the Bronx near Fordham.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: My school's neighborhood is hit very hard by heavy traffic all the time, and a huge number of my students suffer with asthma, and they miss school a lot throughout the year because of that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: My classroom sits on the second floor, right on the front lines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Too often my students smell toxic exhaust in the room, and on these hot days we're stuck between sweating or breathing in fumes with the windows open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Air pollution, as you know, kills over 3,200 New Yorkers every year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: For 50 years, city agencies failed to enforce anti-idling laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: The Citizen Air Complaint Program is the only thing that finally worked.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I know it works because where I live on 36th and 5th in Madison, there is way less idlers than there were three years ago when I started doing this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It's difficult to find them at this point, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It used to be like all the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Yeah, it's great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It actually works.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: So the program is doing its job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: I testified today in strong opposition to Intro 561A, sponsored by Councilmember Gennaro, which relates to regulating engine idling and citizen complaint enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: This intro threatens to wipe out all of our progress and give a massive free pass to corporate polluters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Intro 561A legalizes diesel generation idling, a dirty practice that DEP and OATH have already ruled is illegal and unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It also cuts back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: pay for everyday New Yorkers doing enforcement work, replacing the 50-year-old 25% award with a flat fee, which honestly kind of kills a lot of the incentive for some people, I would think.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It squeezes everyday people reporting pollution the same way delivery apps squeeze gig workers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: In my 16 years of teaching, I've always taught my students to question everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: So I asked the council today, who actually benefits from Intro 561A?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: It's definitely not my students.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: So the problem is pollution, not the people reporting it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Please reject Intro 561A and instead pass Intro 48, sponsored by Councilmember Aviles, which translates the Citizen Air Complaint Program into designated citywide languages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Intro 48 opens up the program to non-English speakers so every New Yorker can help clean air.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: This was good.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so I really appreciate everyone's input.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And, you know, we go forward from here.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I'm a different guy from when I started this hearing.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: So thank you for all the input.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Aaron Jacobs
utterances.text: Thank you as well.

chapters.summary: Gennaro says the last in-person panel has been called and asks whether anyone present still wants to testify. Seeing none, he explains the remote Zoom testimony procedure and says witnesses must wait for the sergeant before speaking.
chapters.title: Gennaro transitions from in-person to remote testimony

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Next panel.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the last in-person panel that I'm going to call now.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That was it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, that was it?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so, you know, we're going to go to remote, you know, Zoom testimony or whatever.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: But if there's anyone.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Isn't that formal language for me to say?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I can just say it in my own words.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yeah, so if anyone here, you know, present, wants to testify before we go to

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: remote testimony, then, you know, now would be the time to come forward, talk to the sergeant, indicating, you know, that you want to testify.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Sort of seeing none, we're going to move over.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Now she's giving me what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We will now turn to remote testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Once your name is called, meaning the people remote, a member of our staff will unmute you, and the sergeant at arms will give you the go-ahead to begin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Please wait for the sergeant to announce that you may begin before delivering your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: If you don't do that, the first part of your testimony is going to be muted.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so that's it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And so now we're going to start.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: And I guess I have to call the witnesses, right?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Alia Sumro.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh, from LCV, of course.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Alia, where are you?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Who says please commence?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Maybe you can.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Maybe Ali is not there.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We can always come back to her.

chapters.summary: Soomro says vehicle idling harms environmental justice neighborhoods near highways and warehouses. NYLCV supports Intro 48 and Intro 11-A, recommends more DEP and OATH resources, and says 561-A is not in the right place, especially its 30-minute school-bus idling allowance.
chapters.title: Alia Soomro of NYLCV supports 48 and 11-A but says 561-A is not ready

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Can y'all hear me now?

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: My name is Alia Sumro, and I'm the Deputy Director for New York City Policy at the New York League of Conservation Voters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Gennaro and members of the committee for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: We're submitting longer written comments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: So every day, thousands of drivers idle their trucks and cars, harming public health and increasing greenhouse gas emissions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Vehicle idling has detrimental cumulative health impacts, especially on environmental justice neighborhoods throughout the city, given the fact that many of these neighborhoods are located near peaker plants, highways, last mile warehouses, and other industrial facilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: The Citizens Air Complaint Program can be a useful tool to combat vehicle idling and improve air quality.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: To improve the program so that the benefits are shared equitably, NYLCV recommends that the submittal process and the interface are more accessible and user-friendly,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: more resources are devoted to DEP, an oath for staffing to process these complaints in a more efficient manner, and the city ramp up enforcement and collections of idling infractions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Additionally, we underscore the importance of working towards comprehensive solutions beyond this program, including but not limited to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: rolling out more neighborhood delivery and loading zones to avoid double and triple parking, utilizing more electric cargo delivery bikes, implementing marine freight delivery such as the Blue Highways program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: And electrifying our school bus fleet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: The city council passed a law several years ago, and we really need to ensure that law is implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: And YLCV has the following thoughts on the bills being heard today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: We support the passage of Intro 48 to make the program more accessible and equitable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: We also support Intro 11A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: And we urge the city to increase idling enforcement and accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: And with that said, we don't think that Intro 561A is in the right place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: For instance, we think that allowing school buses to idle for up to 30 minutes is not right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: It's a little excessive.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Yeah, we'd be happy to work with the council and other stakeholders to improve the program and get it in the right place.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Alia.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: As always, talk soon.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Bye-bye.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Michael McFadden.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We're going to jump down one.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Nandini Ashta Kanasia.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Khaneja says she measured air quality beside operating ice cream trucks and found volatile organic compound spikes at child breathing height. She supports Intro 48, raises concerns about 11-A's penalties for small vendors, and asks the committee to study ice-cream-truck complaints.
chapters.title: Nandini Khaneja presents ice-cream-truck idling measurements

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: My name is Nandini Kanedja.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: I'm a first-year engineering student at Purdue University and a former research intern at CUNY's Advanced Science Research Center Community Sensor Lab.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: I grew up in Queens and Long Island, where ice cream trucks parked outside parks for hours with their engines running, and I was glad to hear an earlier witness describe raising a family in eastern Queens with ice cream trucks idling nearby.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: This summer, I took preliminary measurements of air quality at a young child's breathing height beside operating ice cream trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Over seven visits in Manhattan, my portable sensor tracked volatile organic compounds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: At every visit, the highest reading was 24 to 183% above the visit's typical reading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Neighborhood averages smooth out spikes this short, but a child at the serving window breathes them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: I share the goal of Intro 11, but higher penalties alone concern me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Three violations in three years could cost a vendor $5,000 to $12,000, about the cost of converting a light load truck, one that would have about 16...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: 16 kilowatt hours of power required, and the truck would still run on that fuel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Intro 561 recognizes battery power as a possible remedy through its cure option, but it also writes the processing device exemption that's existed in many other bills of this nature into this code, so many ice cream trucks may never be cited at all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: I estimate that converting one truck avoids about $1,000 to $30,000 a year in health damages, and under a low-tiered rebate, vendors recover their share in three to six and a half years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: As part of today's oversight, I asked the committee to ask DEP how many citizen idling complaints involve ice cream trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: When the committee takes up insurance 635, please amend it to fund compliance and support a 25 truck pilot that measures air quality where children breathe.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: I will follow up with written testimony and supporting calculations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Thank you, and I'm happy to answer any questions.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That was very, very concise and compelling testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You know, we know that you're available for follow up and we appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nandini Khaneja
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, next witness is Hunter Severini.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Severini says idling remains too common and supports higher penalties and language access. He argues 562 would reduce payment rates, 869 raises constitutional concerns, and 561 should be discarded entirely.
chapters.title: Hunter Severini supports 11 and 48 and opposes 561, 562, and 869

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Greetings, my name is Hunter Severini and I'm here to express my strong support for intros 11 and 48, as well as my strongest possible objections to intros 561, 562, and 869.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: The need for intro 11 is obvious because there's still far too much vehicle idling throughout the city under the current penalties, making it clear that they need to be increased.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Intro 48 is equally necessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: More than 20% of the city's population is foreign-born, and requiring the DEP to provide translation on its website would undoubtedly improve public participation, particularly in the outer boroughs, which remain underrepresented in idling complaints.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Website translation is also relatively straightforward to implement these days, making it difficult to argue that this would impose an unreasonable burden on the DEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Intros 561, 562, and 869, on the other hand, appear to offer virtually no meaningful public benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Intro 562 would likely reduce the rate of payment by transferring liability from rental companies, which consistently pay their violations to their customers, who may be much more likely to ignore them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: The current system works, and an idling ticket should not be treated differently from a parking ticket simply because some trucking companies would prefer it that way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Intro 869 is another unnecessary bill because citizen noise complaints have largely ceased to be a significant issue, while a code of conduct

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: raises serious constitutional concerns if it restricts the protected speech of citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: By far the worst bill is Intro 561, and I believe it should be completely discarded.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Its apparent objectives are to reduce the DEP's workload, create opportunities for unscrupulous lawyers to exploit loopholes in the city's air protection laws, and make it easier for commercial vehicles to pollute without facing consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Despite being introduced by Chairman Gennaro, document metadata indicates that the bill was authored by Lisa Alley, a lawyer at the DEP.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: The DP's job is to enforce the law, not weaken it through legislation, and I find the circumstances surrounding Intro 561 deeply concerning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: The agency's apparent involvement in drafting legislation that could undermine its own enforcement responsibilities warrants serious scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Unlike other enforcement agencies, the DP still does not maintain a database of prior offenses searchable by law.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Your time is expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: May I continue a little longer, or is that enough?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Alia Soomro
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Hunter Severini
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness is Douglas Anderson.

chapters.summary: Anderson, president of Anderson Coach and Travel, says one motor coach replaces dozens of cars and that federal safety rules require idling for brakes, lifts, and passenger climate control. He opposes Intro 11 and supports 561.
chapters.title: Doug Anderson says motor coaches are part of the solution

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Good morning, or good afternoon, I should say.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Seems like morning since we started so early.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: I am Doug Anderson, president of Anderson Coach and Travel in Greenville, Pennsylvania, and past chairman of the American Bus Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: And I want to oppose number 11 and support 561.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Motor coaches are part of the solution, not the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: One motor coach gets dozens of cars, less traffic, fewer emissions, and less parking demand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Federal safety rules often require idling for air brakes, accessibility lifts, passenger climates, and no driver should have to choose between city fines and federal safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Passenger safety and comfort is paramount in the charter bus industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: The fine and compliant process is unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: As you've heard earlier, the time between getting fines or getting occurrences and actually getting notification of the occurrences sometimes is up to two years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: We suggest, I suggest, allocating a portion of the fine money to the DEP for staffing so that they could be much more efficient on this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: The economic impact of diminished motor coach tour into the New York City segment city limit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: We donated $12.7 billion in economic impact to the New York City area, 59,200 jobs and $5.9 billion in visitor spending every year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: We want to be partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: We asked the committee to hold the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Introduction number 11, until the compliance process is fixed, enforce equality on public and private fleets.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Write federal safety exemptions clearly into the code and designate legal coach staging and layover spaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Motor coaches bring people to New York City safely and efficiently.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Doug Anderson
utterances.text: Let's help keep doing that.

chapters.summary: Hartman says the real goal is simply to get drivers to turn off engines when not needed. He argues necessary uses are already exempt and that DEP, not the law, is the bottleneck.
chapters.title: Chris Hartman opposes 561-A and says necessary idling is already exempt

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: I was in chambers waiting to testify but had to leave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: I missed a good portion of the testimony after I left.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: I am strongly opposed to 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: In my opinion, seeking to gut the citizen idling program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: It's that simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: No one receives a violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: if their engine is on for any necessary purpose, which we've heard some of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: There's been a lot of misleading testimony about people being given violations when they had some legitimate reason.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: The DEP is really the source of the frustrations from so many people here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: They're simply not performing their tasks as they should.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: And Oath is also fallen greatly behind, but the DEP is the real bottleneck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: I've had tremendous frustration as a citizen trying to make things better for all of our New Yorkers breathing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: And I'm constantly frustrated with the DEP's unwillingness to actually do this task as they should and as they actually require to do that now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Chris Hartman
utterances.text: Stifling.

chapters.summary: Craig says Conservation Law Foundation litigates anti-idling cases, including against Academy Express. She says a Massachusetts court found stationary regeneration especially polluting and that buses can regenerate while driving, so 561-A's exemption is harmful.
chapters.title: Sarah Craig of CLF opposes 561-A's regeneration exemption

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: My name is Sarah Craig and I am a senior attorney with Conservation Law Foundation's Clean Air and Water team.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: I am honored to speak on behalf of CLF and its members in opposing proposed Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: Conservation Law Foundation is a member-supported nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting New England's environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: CLF has engaged in an anti-idling campaign focused on reducing unnecessary idling and the harmful public health and environmental impacts from vehicle exhaust pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: As part of that campaign, we have litigated Clean Air Act cases to stop unnecessary idling by several bus companies serving both New England and New York, including Academy Express.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: CLF's case against Academy went to trial earlier this year in the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: District Court for the District of Massachusetts, and that court found Academy liable for a pattern and practice of violating the Massachusetts anti-idling law and the Clean Air Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: Consistent with the testimony on regeneration we heard earlier today,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: The court found that the process of stationary regeneration is especially polluting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: An employee testimony and evidence produced in our idling cases has all

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: also shown that stationary regeneration creates extremely hot exhaust gases and should be performed away from people.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: The evidence in our idling cases has consistently shown it is possible for bus companies to perform regeneration while a vehicle is driving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: And the court in the Academy case ultimately found that stationary regeneration performed outside of maintenance yards and at random stops along bus routes is neither necessary

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: nor acceptable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Craig
utterances.text: The proposed bill 561A would effectively create a diesel regeneration exemption that encourages drivers to engage in this harmful and especially polluting activity along the New York City streets.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you for your good testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Before I call the next witness, can I just see the sergeant for a second?

utterances.text: Next witness, Jason Chernow.

chapters.summary: Charnes represents the National Limousine Association and a New Jersey chauffeur group. He says operators support clean air but need recognition of passenger safety, climate control, and regeneration needs, and he opposes 11-A.
chapters.title: Jason Charnes opposes Intro 11-A for limousine and motor-coach operators

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: On behalf of the National Limousine Association, the Chauffeur Transportation Association, New Jersey, my name is Jason Charnes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: As I mentioned, we are here in opposition of introduction of number 11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: I serve on the board of directors for both the NLA and the Chauffeur Transportation Association, New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: Let me begin by making one thing clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: Motor coach limousine operators support New Jersey, New York City's clean air goals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: We all have a responsibility to reduce emissions and protect the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: However, we believe the city must distinguish between unnecessary, wasteful idling and legitimate operational needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: We respectfully ask that motor coach and limousine industry associations also be included in developing policies and enforcement practices that balance emissions reductions with passenger safety and the practical realities of our industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: There are several areas of concern with current enforcement initiatives, the enforcement tactics, and proposed increase in penalties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: As you've heard from others today, passenger safety is a major concern.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: Many of our passengers who rely on our services are senior citizens, school-age children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: They are also the core populations that our companies serve, and they deserve safe, reliable, and comfortable transportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: We have serious concerns about the performance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: drivers who are caught in the middle also.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: They expect to balance passenger safety, compliance with idling regulations, company operating policies, vehicle maintenance requirements, the regeneration cycles that are required by modern diesel engines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: These responsibilities do not align neatly with the current way the rules are being enforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: Our members consistently

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: report receiving violations when DOP enforcement officers and participants in the citizen air complaint program do not fully understand the circumstances requiring a vehicle to idle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: A vehicle may need to maintain a safe and comfortable interior temperature for its passengers, or a driver may be preparing to load and unload passengers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: These circumstances deserve to be considered before a violation is issued.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: We have heard from member companies that they instruct drivers.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jason Charnes
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairman, and I will submit my testimony via email as well.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

chapters.summary: Griffith says he has been a bus operator for more than 40 years and has trained thousands of drivers. He argues buses must idle to build air pressure and perform safety checks, and he offers to demonstrate the process to officials.
chapters.title: Anthony Griffith says zero-idling enforcement conflicts with bus safety

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairman and the Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: My name is Anthony Griffith.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: I am a transportation consultant, and I've been a bus operator for over 40 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: The thing that no one is talking about is the zero idling law, which does not allow any idling at all, which makes it impossible for you to safely operate your vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: There is just no way around it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: We need to build up air pressure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: We need to do a lot of things for passenger safety that's not being taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: I've fought many of these idling tickets at court, and they do not care about passenger safety.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: It's not built into their, as they say, it's not part of what the law talks about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: As a bus operator and a trainer, I've trained over 5,000 bus operators.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: And one of the main things that I do is make sure that they follow federal, state, and 19A laws that make sure that they take care of the things that they need to do before attempting to move their vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: Vehicles will not move with low air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: So there are a lot of things that are not being taken into consideration when you go to the idling court and the citizens have no clue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: And one of the things, I'm going to say this real quick, one of the things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: things I'm offering is to put city council members, DEP members, OSTAFF, and any other person that wants to understand truly what it takes to operate a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: I will bring a vehicle and myself as a qualified driver to personally educate you on what it's going to take.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anthony Griffith
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.title: Gawar Eki supports 561-A and 562 but opposes 11-A

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Nice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Thank you for taking the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: This has been a long meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: I've already sent in my written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: So after sitting through this hearing today, let me just briefly say we support Intro 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We support Intro 562.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We're completely against Intro 11A until this program is straightened out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: I'm in the trucking industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We operate around 2,000 trucks in the metro area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We do not operate those trucks except for 12 service trucks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We need Intro 562.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: And I've attended...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Probably hundreds of oath hearings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Here's the big problem here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: However, the DEP kicks it to hub.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: So then we have to identify the customer, get it to the customer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: We cannot just bill them because this is not a red light camera ticket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: This is intended for the lessee, which is a seven, six to seven year term.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: For them to handle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: If they pay it, they pay it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: If they do the hearing or they miss the hearing, then we have to extend it even longer because it goes into default.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: As for Intro 561A, all I hear about is DPF regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: DPF regeneration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: Chairman Gennaro,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: I've been in this business for 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: You have all the information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: But I'll tell you right now, leave it out of the bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: It doesn't affect us either way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki
utterances.text: It's not going to be a defense we're going to use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gawar Eki

chapters.summary: Kane says higher fines burden an already regulated industry and stress drivers. He says ADA lift operations can take 10 to 15 minutes with the engine running and that HVAC and defrosters also require engine operation.
chapters.title: Patrick Kane of Fullington Bus opposes 11-A and cites ADA lift timing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Thank you for your time today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: My name is Patrick Kane.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: I'm the Senior Safety Director for Fullington Bus Company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: I just wanted to point out a few things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: We are in opposition of 11A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: As the operator of a commercial motor vehicle fleet servicing tourism as well as inner city commuters,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: This code poses yet another burden on a high, already highly regulated industry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: From a driver standpoint, we have seen additional stresses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Driving a large commercial vehicle in congested city environments can be a very stressful undertaking.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Drivers now report additional stress created by needing to watch the clock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Drivers also expressed the feeling of needing to rush the passenger loading, unloading, and baggage handling processes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: We would also like to point out that the typical time needed to safely operate an ADA lift and secure a wheelchair is between 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: The vehicle must be running for that process to take place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Secondly, we've seen an increase in passenger complaints regarding cabin temperatures with the heat of summer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: And as you know, we are now working into the winter season.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: In order for the operator to use the HVAC system, the engine must be running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: And this will also affect the heating system, including the windshield defrosters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Lastly, there is additional operating costs with fuel, tolls, licensing, insurances, permits, maintenance costs continuing to rise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: They're always already very thin margins with our additional $6,000 in idling fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Yet the unknown costs in the 12 to 18 month citation processing times, these routes may simply become economically not viable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Should the route become non-viable, this code will have exactly the opposite effect as intended.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: A single motor coach has the potential to eliminate between 50 plus vehicles from the traffic generated into the city every day.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Your time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Patrick.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness is Ann Diebel.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Diebel says she is a private investigator who found the complaint program confusing but has seen it change truck behavior near PS 307. She suggests DEP send rapid warning notices with video links, as other agencies do.
chapters.title: Anne Diebel opposes 561-A and suggests warning notices

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: My name is Anne Diebel, and I'm a private investigator in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: I'm opposed to 561A.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: I've filed fewer than a half a dozen complaints through the Citizen Complaint Program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: Although I have experience in using public records, gathering evidence, and so on, I still found the program difficult and confusing, so I decided to leave the complaints to others.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: But I have followed the program since then and have noticed its effects where I live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: When I used to walk with my daughter next to the local elementary school, PS307, there were lines of dump trucks for days on end, on the entire time, for work on the Con Ed substation and the Navy Yard and for local condo excavation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: These days, if you so much as point a phone at them, they'll shut off.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: And in fact, I've noticed they're often turned off from the get-go, even when the weather is bad.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: The drivers in the same line now dress for the weather and use the site flaggers and WhatsApp groups to call up the trucks one by one instead of inching forward.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: This is clearly the direct impact of the program, not just better air, but better operational efficiency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: It sounds like the program's biggest problem for all parties is processing time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: Other cities like San Bernardino and Reno, as well as departments within NYC,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: like Landmarks Preservation and HPD, rapidly send respondents warnings without asserting that an actual violation has occurred.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: There's no reason DEP can't be set up the same way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anne Diebel
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your good testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness, Brian Gattins, looks like.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Brian Gattins.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, not present.

utterances.text: What do we have next?

utterances.text: Molly Stark Ragsdale.

utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Okay, next witness, Courtney Villani.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.
