utterances.text: Thomas Bailey.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thomas Bailey.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Bailey says he lives in Midtown East and supports the complaint program for quality of life. He opposes 561 and suggests more DEP technology and staff plus public street signage in high-density areas.
chapters.title: Thomas Bailey opposes 561 and suggests more DEP staff and signage

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairman Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: Appreciate you holding this hearing and taking the time to really hear our views.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: I was born in New York City, and I currently live in Midtown East.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: I'm here to express my concerns with 561.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: My support for the Citizens Air Complaint Program comes down to quality of life and keeping New York City a great place to live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: I have great respect for truckers and utility workers and understand that driving in New York is not easy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: Let alone a large truck.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: I also understand these guys are trying to run a business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: But too often, I see giant trucks idling while workers are simply eating a pizza or on their phones while in the truck during a perfectly nice sunny day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: The truck industry representatives have mentioned lift gates and refrigeration units, but each citizen complaint currently must prove to DEP that a lift gate is not in use or a refrigeration unit is independently powered.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: To conclude, my suggestion here is to improve the program as follows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: DEP needs more technology investment as well as more staff members to better handle

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: the high number of violations in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: One additional suggestion is that the city could provide more public street signage indicating that idling is against the law in high density areas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Thomas Bailey
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Bailey.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I appreciate your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness, Andrew Lynch.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Lynch says 561-A's definition of terminal point could make every scheduled bus stop a zero-idling zone. He warns that buses cannot comply because of air-operated systems and wheelchair lifts, and asks the Council to keep terminal point limited to depots and layovers.
chapters.title: Andrew Lynch of Hampton Jitney critiques 561-A's terminal-point definition

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro, members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I'm Andrew Lynch, Executive Vice President of Hampton Jitney.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I fully support eliminating unnecessary idling, and I also fully support cleaner air for New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I'm going to focus on one area of Intro 561A to help with future iterations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Building on what the previous gentleman, the bus driver trainer, was saying, 561A defines terminal point as, quote, the plan stops, including the beginning or end of a bus route.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Read plainly, that is every scheduled bus stop in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: And at a terminal point, idling is not limited to three minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: It is prohibited outright.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Anytime it is above 40 degrees, not one second.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Now, due to our air-operated systems, ambitions, equipment, wheelchair lifts, everything you've heard today, there is no way for our vehicles to comply with zero idling at a stop.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Three minutes is also an issue, but not my point right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: And this is not what terminal point has previously meant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: The existing law describes a terminal point as whether or not enclosed, language that only makes sense if the drafters were talking about a structure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: The terminal point provision was written for a finite known set of places.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: As written, 561A makes it thousands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Think about what that does to enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Make every one of those stops a zero-second idling violation, attach a reward to reporting it, and you have not built the deterrent you want because there is no way for us to be compliant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Instead, you've built another high-volume citizen complaint program that will exist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: exacerbate the criminal oath due process issues we already have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: So do not let Terminal Point become every bus stop in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Keep it to what it has always meant, the terminal, the depot, the layover.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I see that 561A gives school buses 30 minutes of heating and air conditioning to maintain passenger comfort, and we support that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I'll note that it gives a private motor coach carrying those same children on a field trip absolutely nothing, and that does not make sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Your own code already treats buses differently depending on which bus it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Your time is expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: It can be drawn, and it can be drawn correctly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: I have written testimony submitted and be happy to have a further conversation with the committee.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Lynch, thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: That was something I was not aware of, and so you brought some good value added to this proceeding, and I appreciate you for that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Andrew Lynch
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness, Michelle Pedalicki.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Petuliski of Panorama Tours describes buses overheating, regeneration being interrupted, and summonses arriving months later. She asks the Council to exclude private motor coaches from 11-A and the citizen idling program or at least provide timely enforcement and safeguards.
chapters.title: Michelle Petuliski describes motor-coach operational conflicts with idling rules

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Imagine this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: A motor coach drops off 45 students in New York City on an 86-degree day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Hours later, the bus is unbearably hot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Unable to idle long enough to cool it, the driver instead drives the empty 45-foot motor coach around the city with the air conditioning running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: More traffic, more emissions, all to comply with an environmental law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Now imagine this, a motor coach needs to complete a regen cycle to reduce emissions that started while the bus was in motion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: But New York City's idling restrictions scares the driver into not allowing it to complete and turns the bus off mid-process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: The bus derates and cannot be driven home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: It must be towed and replaced with a motor coach dispatched to pick up the passengers, albeit late.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Imagine this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: A $1,000 idling summons arrives 10 months after an alleged violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: The driver has completed hundreds of trips since, camera footage has been overwritten, and the company has virtually no way to defend it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: And imagine this, a group returns from a parade on a hot day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: The driver followed New York City's idling restrictions and didn't run the bus.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: The result, a threat of a one-star Google review criticizing the company for, and I quote, not even caring enough to cool down the bus for the passengers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: These aren't hypothetical scenarios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Every single one of them has happened to my company.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: I'm Michelle Petuliski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: I'm president of Panorama Tours, a family-owned, woman-owned, second-generation motor coach company serving New York City for over 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: I'm also the incoming chair for the Greater Northeast Motor Coach Association and an executive board member for the United Motor Coach Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Our industry cares deeply about the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: We're not here asking for permission to pollute.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: We're asking to recognize that there is a difference between unnecessary idling and operational idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: I urge this committee to exclude private motor coaches from Intro 11A and the broader citizen idling enforcement program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: At a minimum, we need reasonable enforcement timeliness, safeguards against abuse, and fair opportunities to...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: I've written more technological stuff in my written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Michelle Petuliski
utterances.text: And I'm available for anything else.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: We really appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness, Alice.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Alice Mock.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Present.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro

utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Whalen says film and TV production trucks are a mobile factory that needs power for sets. He argues the idling law lacks due process and transparency, produces delayed summonses, and forces drivers to choose between unsafe cabin conditions and fines.
chapters.title: Jim Whalen of Teamsters Local 817 opposes strict idling enforcement for film crews

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: I'm Jim Whalen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: I'm here on behalf of Teams'Local 817, the crew that keeps New York City film and TV industry moving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: When you spot a production crew parked on a New York City street, you might see a bunch of trucks and trailers, but you're actually looking at a mobile factory generating a lot of money for our city and providing good union-paying jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: It's a manufacturing plant on wheels with a massive logistics footprint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: It rolls into neighborhoods overnight, sets up assembly lines for lights, camera, and action, and crafts a final piece of cinemagic art.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: So we are lucky and privileged to use New York City as our studio backlot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Our trucks are packed with specialized equipment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Like any factory, we need large commercial vehicles to transport equipment and provide power for film sets, which brings us to a big hurdle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: New York City's strict anti-idling laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: If you can imagine a regular brick-and-mortar factory that had to shut down every three minutes, it just wouldn't work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: In my opinion, this law lacks due process and transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: There is no immediate notification, sometimes between six to nine months before we see a summons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: With this, it's impossible to gather evidence for a defense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Third, we are seeing deceptive bounty hunter tactics, like filming exempt vehicles while hiding the fact that the lift gate is in use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Plus, the law seems to violate equal protection by shielding city and state-owned vehicles that are usually exempts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Fines usually affect the local small trucking companies that service our industry, as well as major studios that produce film and TV shows.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Our employers are frustrated and have attempted to shift these fines onto our hardworking members of Team SIS Local 817.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: We fully understand the health and environmental perks of cutting emission, but these rigid rules also take a physical toll on our drivers during extreme weather.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: New York winters are freezing and summers are scorching, and yet running an engine for heat or AC isn't an allowed exception.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: For drivers in our industry who spend hours in stationary cabs waiting for the day to end, it's tough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: The law forces a brutal choice to endure unsafe cabin conditions or face steep fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: This is about...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Of operating commercial vehicles in our busy city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jim Whalen
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Whalen.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: I really appreciate you and all the teams.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: and all you do.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: James F. Gennaro
utterances.text: Next witness, Louis Dubouquet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Kane
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Dubuque represents the National Waste and Recycling Association and describes tickets issued during garbage collection and regeneration. He asks the Council to protect active collection, required regeneration, and temporary safety stops.
chapters.title: Lew Dubuque seeks enforcement fixes for waste and recycling trucks

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Gennaro and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: My name is Lou Dubuque, and I'm representing the New York City chapter of the National Waste and Recycling Association.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Our industry supports improving air quality and reducing unnecessary emissions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: However, we have serious concerns about how the city's idling laws are being enforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Let me give you three examples.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: First, our members are receiving idling tickets while actively collecting garbage simply because the compactor blade isn't moving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Does the city really want operators running their compactor blade every three minutes, whether necessary or not, just to avoid a ticket?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: This absolutely makes no sense.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Second, our members have received tickets during diesel particulate filter regeneration, a necessary process that actually reduces emissions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Some have been told to drive back to their yards to complete regeneration, then return to their routes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: How does driving additional miles across the city improve air quality?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: Finally, a member received a ticket while waiting for a car and bicyclist to pass.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: The driver was operating safely and was penalized for it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque
utterances.text: We appreciate the intro of 561A that it had

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lew Dubuque

chapters.summary: Schnell, a pediatrician, says 561-A shows disregard for human health. He urges higher fines, serious enforcement, no discounts for polluters, faster summonses, better OATH training, and a simpler complaint process.
chapters.title: Dr. Patrick Schnell opposes 561-A and lists anti-idling priorities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairman Gennaro.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: My name is Patrick Schnell, and I used to start out my testimonies by stating that I'm a board-certified pediatrician and list the adverse health impact of traffic-related air pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: But I've learned over time that hardly anyone cares about the impact of air pollution on human health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: In fact, Intro 561 is prime evidence for the fact that whoever drafted it is entirely uninterested in the protection of human health, let alone the environment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: To those who will be harmed if this bill passes, it does not matter whether ignorance, negligence, carelessness or corruption are the key drivers behind this bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: What matters and what is clear already today is that significant harm will be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: What is also clear is that this bill will be a stain on the city council and tarnish its legacy for a very long time to come.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: It is really quite simple.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: To stop idling in New York City, we need to do the following.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Number one, increase fines for idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Just adjusting the $350 for inflation would actually result in a $550 fine today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Two, become serious about enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Number three, stop rewarding idling by giving those companies which pollute the most a discount for outstanding fines.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Number four, speed up the issuing of summonses for idling.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: We have made that point many years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: So have the truckers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: And I don't understand why the city cannot get this done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Number five, educate oath hearing officers about relevant basic facts surrounding idling so that respondents'lies will not result in inappropriate dismissals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Number six, simplify the program as much as possible to make it easier for new people to join and to report idlers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Intro 561.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: A proposes to discard violations which have not been processed within 60 days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We've been through that.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Keep going.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: I had to go by what I had when I came up with my testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: There is no time limit to the damage air pollution causes to human health, and there should be none for violating anti-idling laws meant to protect human health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Further, to discard valid idling complaints is fiscally irresponsible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Patrick Schnell
utterances.text: Who develop asthma, heart attacks, strokes.

chapters.summary: Berthet says her pedestrian-safety group CheckPeds works in a neighborhood with some of the city's worst air quality. She says the complaint program reduced idling and urges the Council not to dismantle a successful system.

summary: The Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts held an oversight and legislative hearing on DEP's citizen enforcement programs and six idling, noise, and language-access bills.
DEP, OATH, and the Department of Finance declined to appear; Chair Gennaro read DEP's written testimony into the record while environmental, industry, labor, and resident witnesses testified.
Testimony centered on idling health impacts, complaint backlog and due process, language access, diesel regeneration exemptions, and whether Intro 561-A should be amended or rejected.
title: Committee on Environmental Protection and Waterfronts
